title.zh: 卷三百〇一 列傳第一百八十九 列女一
title.raw: 卷三百〇一 列傳第一百八十九 列女一 Volume 301 Biographies 189: Exemplary Women 1

sentences.zh: 婦人之行，不出於閨門，故《詩》載《關雎》、《葛覃》、《桃夭》、《芣苜》，皆處常履順，貞靜和平，而內行之修，王化之行，具可考見。

translations.literal: The conduct of women does not go beyond the inner chambers; therefore the Book of Songs records "Guan Ju," "Ge Tan," "Tao Yao," and "Fu Yi" — all exemplify dwelling in ordinary life, following the proper path, chastity, tranquility, and harmony — and the cultivation of inner virtue and the practice of royal transformation can all be examined and seen.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's conduct was not meant to extend beyond the domestic sphere. The Book of Songs therefore celebrates such poems as "Guan Ju," "Ge Tan," "Tao Yao," and "Fu Yi," all of which show women living in their everyday roles with propriety, chastity, quiet grace, and harmony — through which one can trace both the cultivation of private virtue and the workings of royal moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 其變者，《行露》、《柏舟》，一二見而已。

translations.literal: As for variations, "Xing Lu" and "Bo Zhou" appear only once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: Departures from this norm — such as "Xing Lu" and "Bo Zhou" — appear only once or twice.

sentences.zh: 劉向傳列女，取行事可為鑒戒，不存一操。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang in his Biographies of Exemplary Women selected conduct that could serve as a mirror and warning, without preserving a single standard of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In his Biographies of Exemplary Women, Liu Xiang chose stories that could serve as examples and warnings, rather than holding up one fixed model of conduct.

sentences.zh: 範氏宗之，亦采才行高秀者，非獨貴節烈也。

translations.literal: Fan Ye followed his approach, also selecting women of lofty talent and virtue, not honoring chastity and martyrdom alone.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye adopted the same approach, also gathering accounts of women distinguished by talent and character — not valuing chastity and heroic sacrifice alone.

sentences.zh: 魏、隋而降，史家乃多取患難顛沛、殺身殉義之事。

translations.literal: From the Wei and Sui dynasties onward, historians came to draw mostly on accounts of hardship and destitution, of giving one's life in devotion to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Sui dynasties onward, historians tended to record chiefly stories of women who endured hardship and destitution, or who gave their lives in sacrifice for duty.

sentences.zh: 蓋挽近之情，忽庸行而尚奇激，國制所褒，誌乘所錄，與夫裏巷所稱道，流俗所震駭，胥以至奇至苦為難能。

translations.literal: This was because sentiments of recent times slighted ordinary conduct and prized the extraordinary and dramatic; what the state's regulations honored, what local gazetteers recorded, what lanes and alleys praised, and what common opinion found startling — all alike regarded the most extraordinary and most painful as the most difficult achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times, ordinary virtue had come to seem unremarkable while the sensational and extreme were admired. What the state honored, what gazetteers recorded, what neighbors praised in the streets, and what common people found shocking — all treated the most extraordinary and agonizing deeds as the highest achievements.

sentences.zh: 而文人墨客往往借俶儻非常之行，以發其偉麗激越跌宕可喜之思，故其傳尤遠，而其事尤著。

translations.literal: Moreover, literary men often borrowed unorthodox and extraordinary acts to express their grand, impassioned, and stirring thoughts worth savoring; hence such biographies spread especially far, and such deeds became especially prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and writers often seized on these unconventionally heroic acts to give voice to grand, impassioned, and emotionally stirring ideas — which is why such stories spread especially widely and these deeds became especially famous.

sentences.zh: 然至性所存，倫常所系，正氣之不至於淪澌，而斯人之所以異於禽獸，載筆者宜莫之敢忽也。

translations.literal: Yet the innate sincerity that remains, the human relations and constants to which it is bound, the righteous spirit that does not sink into dissolution, and the reason such people differ from birds and beasts — those who wield the brush ought not to dare neglect any of these.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deepest human feeling, the bonds of moral obligation, the righteous spirit that keeps society from decay, and what distinguishes humanity from beasts — none of these should be lightly dismissed by any historian who takes up the brush.

sentences.zh: 明興，著為規條，巡方督學歲上其事。

translations.literal: When the Ming dynasty rose, this was established as regulation; touring provincial education commissioners reported such cases annually.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty was founded, regulations were drawn up requiring regional education commissioners to report such cases to the throne each year.

sentences.zh: 大者賜祠祀，次亦樹坊表，烏頭綽楔，照耀井閭，乃至僻壤下戶之女，亦能以貞白自砥。

translations.literal: In major cases, temples and sacrifices were granted; in lesser ones, memorial arches were erected — black-painted pillars and inscribed tablets shining upon lanes and neighborhoods — so that even daughters of humble households in remote regions could temper themselves through chastity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the most notable cases, the state granted temples and sacrifices; in lesser ones, memorial arches were raised with painted pillars and inscribed plaques that lit up entire neighborhoods — so that even women from poor families in out-of-the-way places could uphold chastity and integrity as their standard.

sentences.zh: 其著於實錄及郡邑誌者，不下萬余人，雖間有以文藝顯，要之節烈為多。

translations.literal: Those recorded in the Veritable Records and county and prefectural gazetteers numbered no fewer than ten thousand; although some gained renown through literary talent, for the most part chastity and martyrdom predominated.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand such women were recorded in the Veritable Records and local gazetteers. Although a few became known for literary achievement, chastity and heroic sacrifice were by far the most common themes.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 何其盛也。

translations.literal: How flourishing it was.
translations.idiomatic: How abundant this was.

sentences.zh: 豈非聲教所被，廉恥之分明，故名節重而蹈義勇歟！

translations.literal: Was this not because civilization's influence spread everywhere, and shame and honor were clearly distinguished, so that reputation and virtue were held in weight and the pursuit of righteousness was undertaken with courage!
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because moral teaching had reached every corner of the realm, shame and honor were clearly defined, and women therefore held reputation and integrity dear and met duty with courage!

sentences.zh: 今掇其尤者，或以年次，或以類從，具著於篇，視前史殆將倍之。

translations.literal: Now the most outstanding cases are gathered — some arranged chronologically, some grouped by category — and fully set forth in this chapter; compared with earlier histories, the number is nearly doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Here I have selected the most notable cases, arranged partly by chronology and partly by category, and set them out fully in this chapter — nearly twice as many as appear in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 然而姓名湮滅者，尚不可勝計，存其什一，亦足以示勸雲。

translations.literal: Yet those whose names have been lost still cannot be fully counted; to preserve one tenth of them is enough to serve as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet countless others have vanished into oblivion; to preserve even a tenth of them should be encouragement enough.

sentences.zh: 月娥，西域人，元武昌尹職馬祿丁女也。

translations.literal: Yue'e was a native of the Western Regions, the daughter of Zhima Luding, who had been prefect of Wuchang under the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue'e came from the Western Regions. She was the daughter of Zhima Luding, who had served as prefect of Wuchang under the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧，聽諸兄誦說經史，輒通大義。

translations.literal: From youth she was intelligent; when she heard her elder brothers recite the classics and histories, she immediately grasped their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was bright and quick-witted. Whenever she heard her elder brothers reciting the classics and histories, she immediately understood their meaning.

sentences.zh: 長適蕪湖葛通甫，事上撫下，一秉禮法。

translations.literal: When she grew up she married Ge Tongfu of Wuhu; in serving those above and caring for those below, she held fast to ritual and law throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she married Ge Tongfu of Wuhu. In her dealings with superiors and inferiors alike, she adhered strictly to propriety.

sentences.zh: 長姒盧率諸婦女，悉受其教。

translations.literal: Her elder sister-in-law Lu led the other women, and all received her instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister-in-law Lu led the other women of the household, and all of them looked to Yue'e for guidance.

sentences.zh: 太祖渡江之六年，偽漢兵自上遊而下，盧曰：「太平有城郭，且嚴兵守，可恃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year after the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangtze, the armies of the false Han came down from upstream. Lu said: "Taiping has walls and ramparts, and its garrison is strong — we can rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year after the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangtze, the armies of the false Han advanced from upstream. Lu said, "Taiping has walls and a strong garrison — we can take refuge there.

sentences.zh: 」使月娥挾諸婦女往避之。

translations.literal: " She had Yue'e take the women there to seek refuge.
translations.idiomatic: " She sent Yue'e to escort the women there for safety.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇至，城陷，月娥嘆曰：「吾生詩禮家，可失節於賊邪！

translations.literal: Before long the bandits arrived and the city fell. Yue'e sighed and said: "I was born into a family of poetry and ritual — how could I lose my chastity to bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy arrived and the city fell. Yue'e sighed and said, "I was born into a family steeped in the classics — how could I surrender my honor to bandits!

sentences.zh: 」抱幼女赴水死。

translations.literal: " She clasped her infant daughter and drowned herself in the water.
translations.idiomatic: " She took her infant daughter in her arms and drowned herself in the river.

sentences.zh: 諸婦女相從投水者九人，方盛暑，屍七日不浮，顏色如生。

translations.literal: Nine women followed her into the water; though it was the height of summer, their bodies did not float for seven days, and their complexions were as if they were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Nine other women followed her into the water. Though it was the height of summer, their bodies did not rise to the surface for seven days, and their faces looked as lifelike as before.

sentences.zh: 鄉人為巨穴合葬之故居之南，題曰十女墓。

translations.literal: The villagers dug a great pit and buried them together south of their former residence, inscribing the site as the Tomb of the Ten Women.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers dug a large communal grave south of their former home and buried them together, marking the site as the Tomb of the Ten Women.

sentences.zh: 娥弟丁鶴年，幼通經史，皆娥口授也。

translations.literal: Yue'e's younger brother Ding Henian mastered the classics and histories in youth — all through instruction received orally from Yue'e.
translations.idiomatic: Yue'e's younger brother Ding Henian mastered the classics and histories as a boy — all through lessons Yue'e taught him by word of mouth.

sentences.zh: 後通甫與盧皆死於寇。

translations.literal: Later both Tongfu and Lu died at the hands of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Later both Tongfu and Lu were killed by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 劉孝婦，新樂韓太初妻。

translations.literal: Liu the Filial Wife was the wife of Han Taichu of Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu the Filial Wife was the wife of Han Taichu of Xinle.

sentences.zh: 太初，元時為知印。

translations.literal: Taichu had served as seal-keeper under the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu had served as a seal-keeper under the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，例徙和州，挈家行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign, by regulation they were relocated to Hezhou, and the whole family set out.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongwu reign, they were relocated to Hezhou by official decree, and the whole family set out together.

sentences.zh: 劉事姑謹，姑道病，刺血和藥以進。

translations.literal: Liu served her mother-in-law with care; when the old lady fell ill on the road, Liu drew her own blood and mixed it with medicine to offer her.
translations.idiomatic: Liu served her mother-in-law devotedly. When the old lady fell ill on the journey, Liu drew her own blood and mixed it with medicine for her to take.

sentences.zh: 抵和州，夫卒，劉種蔬給姑食。

translations.literal: When they reached Hezhou, her husband died; Liu planted vegetables to provide food for her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Hezhou, her husband died. Liu planted vegetables to provide food for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 越二年，姑患風疾不能起，晝夜奉湯藥，驅蚊蠅不離側。

translations.literal: Two years later, her mother-in-law was stricken with wind paralysis and could not rise; day and night Liu attended her with broth and medicine, driving away mosquitoes and flies and never leaving her side.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, her mother-in-law was stricken with paralysis and could no longer get up. Day and night Liu tended her with broth and medicine, shooing away mosquitoes and flies and never leaving her side.

sentences.zh: 姑體腐，蛆生席間，為嚙蛆，蛆不復生。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law's body rotted, maggots bred among the bedding; she would bite the maggots, and they ceased to breed.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law's body was rotting and maggots bred in the bedding. Liu would bite them away, and they stopped appearing.

sentences.zh: 及姑疾篤，刲肉食之，少蘇，逾月而卒，殯之舍側。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law's illness grew grave, she cut flesh from her own body for the old lady to eat; the mother-in-law revived slightly, but after more than a month died and was interred beside the dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law's illness turned critical, Liu cut flesh from her own body for the old lady to eat. The mother-in-law rallied briefly, but died a month later and was buried beside the house.

sentences.zh: 欲還葬舅冢，力不能舉喪，哀號五載。

translations.literal: She wished to return and bury her at her husband's father's tomb, but lacked the strength to conduct the funeral; she wailed in grief for five years.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to return her remains for burial at her father-in-law's tomb, but lacked the means to conduct the funeral and wailed in grief for five years.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，遣中使賜衣一襲、鈔二十錠，命有司還其喪，旌門閭，復徭役。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard of it and sent a palace envoy to bestow one suit of clothing and twenty ingots of paper money, ordering the authorities to return the remains for burial, honoring her gate and lane, and exempting her from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu heard of it and sent a palace envoy with one suit of clothing and twenty ingots of paper money, ordering the authorities to return the remains for proper burial, honoring her household with an official commendation, and exempting her from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 同時甄氏，欒城李大妻，事姑孝。

translations.literal: At the same time there was the Zhen clan — the wife of Li Da of Luancheng — who served her mother-in-law with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Lady Zhen, wife of Li Da of Luancheng, who served her mother-in-law with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 姑壽九十一卒，甄廬墓三年，旦暮悲號，亦被旌。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law lived to ninety-one and died; Zhen kept vigil at the tomb for three years, weeping morning and evening, and she too received an official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law lived to ninety-one and died. Zhen kept vigil at the tomb for three years, weeping morning and evening, and she too received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 孝女諸娥，山陰人。

translations.literal: Zhu E the Filial Daughter was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu E the Filial Daughter was a native of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父士吉，洪武初為糧長。

translations.literal: Her father Shi Ji served as grain head in the early Hongwu period.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shi Ji served as grain head in the early Hongwu period.

sentences.zh: 有黠而逋賦者，誣士吉於官，論死，二子炳、煥亦罹罪。

translations.literal: A cunning man who had evaded tax payments falsely accused Shi Ji to the authorities; Shi Ji was sentenced to death, and his two sons Bing and Huan also suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A cunning tax evader falsely accused Shi Ji to the authorities. Shi Ji was sentenced to death, and his two sons Bing and Huan were also punished.

sentences.zh: 娥方八歲，晝夜號哭，與舅陶山長走京師訴冤。

translations.literal: E was only eight years old; day and night she wailed and wept, and with her maternal uncle Tao the district elder she traveled to the capital to plead their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: E was only eight years old. Day and night she wailed and wept, and with her maternal uncle Tao the district elder she traveled to the capital to plead their injustice.

sentences.zh: 時有令，冤者非臥釘板，勿與勘問。

translations.literal: At the time there was a regulation: those claiming wrongful conviction would not be granted an inquiry unless they lay upon a bed of nails.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a regulation that those claiming wrongful conviction would not be granted an inquiry unless they lay upon a bed of nails.

sentences.zh: 娥輾轉其上，幾斃，事乃聞，勘之，僅戍一兄而止。

translations.literal: E rolled upon it until nearly dead; only then was the matter heard. Upon investigation, only one brother was sentenced to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: E rolled upon it until she nearly died. Only then was the matter heard. Upon investigation, only one brother was sentenced to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 娥重傷卒，裏人哀之，肖像配曹娥廟。

translations.literal: E died of her grievous wounds. The townspeople mourned her and placed her portrait in the shrine to Lady Cao E.
translations.idiomatic: E died of her grievous wounds. The townspeople mourned her and placed her portrait in the shrine to Lady Cao E.

sentences.zh: 唐方妻，浙新昌丁氏女，名錦孥。

translations.literal: The wife of Tang Fang was a daughter of the Ding clan of Xinchang in Zhejiang, named Jinnu.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Tang Fang was a daughter of the Ding clan of Xinchang in Zhejiang, named Jinnu.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，方為山東僉事，坐法死，妻子當沒為官婢。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu era, Fang served as administration commissioner of Shandong; convicted under the law he was put to death, and his wife and children were to be confiscated as government bondwomen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era, Fang served as administration commissioner of Shandong. Convicted under the law, he was put to death, and his wife and children were to be confiscated as government bondwomen.

sentences.zh: 有司按籍取之，監護者見丁色美，借梳掠發，丁以梳擲地，其人取掠之，持還丁。

translations.literal: The authorities took them according to the registry. A guard saw that Ding was beautiful and borrowed a comb to smooth her hair; Ding threw the comb to the ground. The man picked it up, smoothed her hair again, and returned the comb to Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities took them according to the registry. A guard saw that Ding was beautiful and borrowed a comb to arrange her hair. Ding threw the comb to the ground. The man picked it up, combed her hair again, and handed the comb back to her.

sentences.zh: 丁罵不受，謂家人曰：「此輩無禮，必辱我，非死無以全節。

translations.literal: Ding cursed him and refused it, saying to her family: "These men are without propriety and will surely dishonor me; only death can preserve my chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Ding cursed him and refused, saying to her family, "These men are without propriety and will surely dishonor me. Only death can preserve my chastity.

sentences.zh: 」肩輿過陰澤，崖峭水深，躍出赴水，衣厚不能沈，從容以手斂裙，隨流而沒，年二十八，時稱其處為夫人潭。

translations.literal: " While carried in a sedan chair past Yin Marsh, where the cliffs were steep and the water deep, she leaped out and threw herself into the water. Her clothes were thick and she could not sink; calmly she gathered her skirt with her hands and drifted with the current until she drowned. She was twenty-eight years old, and the place came to be known as Lady's Pool.
translations.idiomatic: " While being carried in a sedan chair past Yin Marsh, where the cliffs were steep and the water deep, she leaped out and threw herself into the water. Her clothes were thick and she could not sink; calmly she gathered her skirt with her hands and drifted with the current until she drowned. She was twenty-eight, and the place came to be known as Lady's Pool.

sentences.zh: 鄭煁妻石氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Zheng Chen was of the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Zheng Chen was of the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 煁，浦江鄭泳孫也。

translations.literal: Chen was the grandson of Zheng Yong of Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the grandson of Zheng Yong of Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，李文忠薦諸朝，屢遷藏庫提點，坐法死。

translations.literal: In the early Hongwu period, Li Wenzhong recommended him to the court; after repeated promotions he became director of the treasury depot, but was convicted under the law and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Hongwu period, Li Wenzhong recommended him to the court. After repeated promotions he became director of the treasury depot, but was convicted under the law and put to death.

sentences.zh: 石當遣配，泣曰：「我義門婦也，可辱身以辱門乎！

translations.literal: Shi was to be sent away for reassignment. Weeping, she said: "I am a wife of the House of Righteousness — how could I dishonor my own person and thereby dishonor the clan!
translations.idiomatic: Shi was to be sent away for reassignment. Weeping, she said, "I am a wife of the House of Righteousness — how could I dishonor myself and thereby dishonor the clan!

sentences.zh: 」不食死。

translations.literal: " She starved herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " She starved herself to death.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，慈谿人，字同邑鄭子來。

translations.literal: Yang was a native of Cixi and was betrothed to Zheng Zilai of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was a native of Cixi and was betrothed to Zheng Zilai of the same district.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，子來父仲徽戍雲南。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu era, Zilai's father Zhonghui was garrisoned in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era, Zilai's father Zhonghui was garrisoned in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 明制，子成丁者隨遣，子來亦在戍中。

translations.literal: Under Ming regulations, sons who reached adulthood were sent along; Zilai was also among the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming regulations, sons who reached adulthood were sent along with their fathers, and Zilai was also among the garrison.

sentences.zh: 楊年甫十六，聞子來母老弟幼，請於父母，適鄭養姑，以待子來之返。

translations.literal: Yang was only sixteen. Learning that Zilai's mother was elderly and his younger brothers still children, she asked permission of her parents to marry into the Zheng family and nurse her mother-in-law, awaiting Zilai's return.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was only sixteen. Learning that Zilai's mother was elderly and his younger brothers still children, she asked her parents' permission to marry into the Zheng family and care for her mother-in-law while awaiting Zilai's return.

sentences.zh: 子來竟卒戍所，楊與姑撫諸叔成立，以夫從子孔武為嗣，苦節五十余年。

translations.literal: Zilai ultimately died at the garrison. Yang and her mother-in-law raised the younger brothers-in-law to maturity, taking Kongwu, her husband's younger cousin, as heir, and she maintained her chaste widowhood for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Zilai ultimately died at the garrison. Yang and her mother-in-law raised the younger brothers-in-law to maturity, taking Kongwu, her husband's younger cousin, as heir. She maintained her chaste widowhood for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 其後，鄭煥妻張氏，嫁未旬日；

translations.literal: Thereafter there was Zhang, wife of Zheng Huan, who had been married less than ten days;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter there was Lady Zhang, wife of Zheng Huan, who had been married less than ten days;

sentences.zh: 泰然妻嚴氏生子一蘭，方孩抱；

translations.literal: Lady Yan, wife of Tairan, who gave birth to a son named Yilan when he was still an infant in arms;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan, wife of Tairan, who gave birth to a son named Yilan while he was still an infant in arms;

sentences.zh: 栻妻王氏事夫癇病，狂不省人事，服勤八年弗怠；

translations.literal: Lady Wang, wife of Shi, who nursed her husband through epilepsy so severe he was delirious and insensible — serving him diligently for eight years without slackening;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, wife of Shi, who nursed her husband through epilepsy so severe that he was delirious and insensible, serving him diligently for eight years without slackening;

sentences.zh: 三人皆楊氏夫族，先後早寡，皆以節聞。

translations.literal: All three belonged to Yang's husband's clan, were widowed early one after another, and were all known for their chastity.
translations.idiomatic: All three belonged to Yang's husband's clan, were widowed early one after another, and were all known for their chastity.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，知府鄒希賢題曰鄭氏節門，以比浦江鄭氏義門雲。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, prefect Zou Xixian inscribed the phrase "Gateway of Chastity of the Zheng Clan" to compare them with the House of Righteousness of the Zheng clan of Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, prefect Zou Xixian inscribed the phrase "Gateway of Chastity of the Zheng Clan" to compare them with the House of Righteousness of the Zheng clan of Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 貞女韓氏，保寧人。

translations.literal: The chaste maiden Han was a native of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste maiden Han was a native of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 元末明玉珍據蜀，貞女慮見掠，偽為男子服，混跡民間。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, Ming Yuzhen held Sichuan; fearing she would be seized, the chaste maiden disguised herself in men's clothing and mingled among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, Ming Yuzhen held Sichuan. Fearing she would be seized, the chaste maiden disguised herself in men's clothing and mingled among the common people.

sentences.zh: 既而被驅入伍，轉戰七年，人莫知其處女也。

translations.literal: Before long she was conscripted into the army and fought for seven years; no one knew she was a maiden.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she was conscripted into the army and fought for seven years, and no one knew she was a maiden.

sentences.zh: 後從玉珍破雲南還，遇其叔父贖歸成都，始改裝而行，同時從軍者莫不驚異。

translations.literal: Later, returning with Ming Yuzhen after the conquest of Yunnan, she met her uncle who ransomed her back to Chengdu; only then did she change back to women's dress, and her fellow soldiers were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Later, returning with Ming Yuzhen after the conquest of Yunnan, she met her uncle, who ransomed her back to Chengdu. Only then did she change back to women's dress, and her fellow soldiers were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年嫁為尹氏婦。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 4 she married and became a daughter-in-law of the Yin clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 (1371) she married and became a daughter-in-law of the Yin clan.

sentences.zh: 成都人以韓貞女稱。

translations.literal: The people of Chengdu called her Han the Chaste Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chengdu called her Han the Chaste Maiden.

sentences.zh: 其後有黃善聰者，南京人。

translations.literal: Thereafter there was Huang Shancong, a native of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter there was Huang Shancong, a native of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 年十三失母，父販香廬、鳳間，令善聰為男子裝從遊數年。

translations.literal: At thirteen she lost her mother. Her father sold incense between Lushan and Fengyang and had Shancong travel in men's dress with him for several years.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she lost her mother. Her father sold incense between Lushan and Fengyang and had Shancong travel in men's dress with him for several years.

sentences.zh: 父死，善聰習其業，變姓名曰張勝。

translations.literal: When her father died, Shancong mastered the trade and changed her name to Zhang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died, Shancong mastered the trade and changed her name to Zhang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 有李英者，亦販香，與為伴侶者逾年，不知其為女也。

translations.literal: There was a Li Ying who also sold incense; he was her companion for more than a year without knowing she was a woman.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Li Ying who also sold incense. He was her companion for more than a year without knowing she was a woman.

sentences.zh: 後偕返南京省其姊。

translations.literal: Later they returned together to Nanjing to visit her elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Later they returned together to Nanjing to visit her elder sister.

sentences.zh: 姊初不之識，詰知其故，怒詈曰：「男女亂群，辱我甚矣。

translations.literal: Her sister at first did not recognize her; questioning her and learning the reason, she reviled her in anger: "Mixing men and women in the same company — you have shamed me deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister at first did not recognize her. Questioning her and learning the reason, she reviled her in anger, "Mixing men and women in the same company — you have shamed me deeply.

sentences.zh: 」拒不納。

translations.literal: " She refused to take her in.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused to take her in.

sentences.zh: 善聰以死自誓。

translations.literal: Shancong vowed she would die before yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Shancong vowed she would die before yielding.

sentences.zh: 乃呼鄰嫗察之，果處子也。

translations.literal: Her sister then summoned a neighbor woman to examine her; she proved indeed to be a virgin.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister then summoned a neighbor woman to examine her, and she proved indeed to be a virgin.

sentences.zh: 相持痛哭，立為改裝。

translations.literal: They embraced and wept together, and immediately restored her to women's dress.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept together, and immediately restored her to women's dress.

sentences.zh: 明日，英來，知為女，怏怏如失，歸告母求婚。

translations.literal: The next day Ying came; learning she was a woman, he was downcast as if bereft and returned home to tell his mother and ask for her hand in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ying came. Learning she was a woman, he was downcast as if bereft and returned home to tell his mother and ask for her hand in marriage.

sentences.zh: 善聰不從，曰：「若歸英，如瓜李何？

translations.literal: Shancong refused, saying: "If I marry Ying, what of the melon-and-plum reproach?
translations.idiomatic: Shancong refused, saying, "If I marry Ying, what of the melon-and-plum reproach?

sentences.zh: 」鄰裏交勸，執益堅。

translations.literal: " Neighbors and townsfolk all urged her, but she grew only more resolute.
translations.idiomatic: " Neighbors and townsfolk all urged her, but she grew only more resolute.

sentences.zh: 有司聞之，助以聘，判為夫婦。

translations.literal: The local authorities heard of it, assisted with the betrothal gifts, and officially united them as husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities heard of it, assisted with the betrothal gifts, and officially united them as husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 姚孝女，余姚人，適吳氏。

translations.literal: Yao the Filial Daughter was a native of Yuyao and married into the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao the Filial Daughter was a native of Yuyao and married into the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 母出汲，虎銜之去，女追掣虎尾，虎欲前，女掣益力，尾遂脫，虎負痛躍去。

translations.literal: When her mother went out to draw water, a tiger seized her and carried her off. The daughter pursued and grasped the tiger's tail; as the tiger tried to advance, she pulled harder until the tail came off, and the tiger, writhing in pain, leaped away.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother went out to draw water, a tiger seized her and carried her off. The daughter pursued and grasped the tiger's tail. As the tiger tried to advance, she pulled harder until the tail came off, and the tiger, writhing in pain, leaped away.

sentences.zh: 負母還，藥之獲愈，奉其母二十年。

translations.literal: She carried her mother back, treated her with medicine until she recovered, and supported her mother for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: She carried her mother back, treated her with medicine until she recovered, and supported her mother for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 後成化間，武康有蔡孝女，隨母入山采藥。

translations.literal: Later, during the Chenghua reign, in Wukang there was Cai the Filial Daughter, who accompanied her mother into the mountains to gather herbs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Chenghua reign, in Wukang there was Cai the Filial Daughter, who accompanied her mother into the mountains to gather herbs.

sentences.zh: 虎攫其母，女折樹枝格鬥三百余步。

translations.literal: A tiger seized her mother; the daughter fought with a broken tree branch for more than three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger seized her mother, and the daughter fought it with a broken tree branch for more than three hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 虎舍其母，傷女，血歕丈許，竹葉為赤，女亦獲全。

translations.literal: The tiger released her mother but wounded the daughter; blood spurted more than a zhang, turning the bamboo leaves red, yet the daughter also escaped intact.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger released her mother but wounded the daughter. Blood spurted more than a zhang, turning the bamboo leaves red, yet the daughter also escaped unharmed.

sentences.zh: 後招遠有孝女，不知其姓。

translations.literal: Later in Zhaoyuan there was a filial daughter whose surname is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Zhaoyuan there was a filial daughter whose surname is unknown.

sentences.zh: 父采石南山，為蟒所吞。

translations.literal: Her father was quarrying stone on South Mountain when he was swallowed by a python.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was quarrying stone on South Mountain when he was swallowed by a python.

sentences.zh: 女哭之，願見父屍同死。

translations.literal: The daughter wept and wished to see her father's corpse and die with him.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter wept and wished to see her father's corpse and die with him.

sentences.zh: 俄頃大雷電擊蟒墮女前，腹裂見父屍。

translations.literal: In a moment great thunder and lightning struck the python, which fell before the daughter; its belly split open, revealing her father's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment great thunder and lightning struck the python, which fell before the daughter. Its belly split open, revealing her father's corpse.

sentences.zh: 女負土掩埋，觸石而死。

translations.literal: The daughter carried earth to bury him and, striking a stone, died.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter carried earth to bury him and, striking a stone, died.

sentences.zh: 盧佳娘，福清李廣妻。

translations.literal: Lu Jianiang was the wife of Li Guang of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianiang was the wife of Li Guang of Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 婚甫十月，廣暴卒，盧慟絕復蘇，見廣口鼻出惡血，悉餂食之。

translations.literal: They had been married barely ten months when Guang died suddenly. Lu swooned and revived; seeing foul blood issue from Guang's nose and mouth, she licked it all up.
translations.idiomatic: They had been married barely ten months when Guang died suddenly. Lu swooned and revived. Seeing foul blood issue from Guang's nose and mouth, she licked it all up.

sentences.zh: 既殮，哭輒僵仆，積五六日，家人防懈，潛入寢室自經。

translations.literal: After the encoffining, whenever she wept she would stiffen and collapse. After five or six days, when the family's vigil slackened, she stole into the bedchamber and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffining, whenever she wept she would stiffen and collapse. After five or six days, when the family's vigil slackened, she stole into the bedchamber and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 後其縣有遊政妻倪氏殉夫，亦然。

translations.literal: Later in the same county, Ni, wife of You Zheng, followed her husband in death — the same story.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the same county, Ni, wife of You Zheng, followed her husband in death — the same story.

sentences.zh: 又有施氏，滁州彭禾妻。

translations.literal: There was also Lady Shi, wife of Peng He of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Shi, wife of Peng He of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，禾得疾不起，握手訣曰：「疾憊甚，知必死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, He fell gravely ill and could not rise. Taking her hand in farewell he said: "My illness is grievous; I know I must die.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, He fell gravely ill and could not rise. Taking her hand in farewell he said, "My illness is grievous; I know I must die.

sentences.zh: 汝無子，擇婿而嫁，毋守死，徒自苦也。

translations.literal: You have no son — choose a husband and remarry; do not keep vigil unto death, wasting yourself in vain suffering.
translations.idiomatic: You have no son — choose a husband and remarry. Do not keep vigil unto death, wasting yourself in vain suffering.

sentences.zh: 」施泣曰：「君尚不知妾乎！

translations.literal: " Shi wept and said: "Do you still not know your humble wife!
translations.idiomatic: " Shi wept and said, "Do you still not know your humble wife!

sentences.zh: 願先君死。

translations.literal: I wish to die before my lord.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to die before my lord.

sentences.zh: 」禾固止之，因取禾所嘔血盡吞之，以見誌。

translations.literal: " He firmly tried to dissuade her; she then took all the blood He had vomited and swallowed it whole, to show her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " He firmly tried to dissuade her, but she then took all the blood He had vomited and swallowed it whole to show her resolve.

sentences.zh: 及禾歿，即自經。

translations.literal: When He died, she hanged herself at once.
translations.idiomatic: When He died, she hanged herself at once.

sentences.zh: 吳氏，潞州廩生盧清妻。

translations.literal: Wu was the wife of Lu Qing, a stipend student of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was the wife of Lu Qing, a stipend student of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 舅姑歿於臨洺，寄瘞旅次。

translations.literal: Her husband's parents died at Linming and were provisionally interred at an inn along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's parents died at Linming and were provisionally interred at an inn along the way.

sentences.zh: 清授徒自給，後失廩，充掾於汴，憤恥發狂死。

translations.literal: Qing supported himself by teaching; later he lost his stipend and served as a clerk in Bianliang, where shame and humiliation drove him mad and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qing supported himself by teaching. Later he lost his stipend and served as a clerk in Bianliang, where shame and humiliation drove him mad and he died.

sentences.zh: 吳聞訃，痛絕，哭曰：「吾舅姑委骨於北，良人死，忍令終不返乎！

translations.literal: When Wu heard the news she swooned in grief and wept: "My husband's parents left their bones in the north, and now my husband is dead — how can I bear to let them never return!
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard the news she swooned in grief and wept, "My husband's parents left their bones in the north, and now my husband is dead — how can I bear to let them never return!

sentences.zh: 」乃寄幼孤於姊兄，鬻次女為資，獨抵臨洺，覓舅姑瘞處不得，號泣中野。

translations.literal: " She entrusted her young orphan to her elder sister and brother, sold her second daughter for funds, and traveled alone to Linming. Unable to find where her in-laws had been interred, she wailed and wept in the open wilds.
translations.idiomatic: " She entrusted her young orphan to her elder sister and brother, sold her second daughter for funds, and traveled alone to Linming. Unable to find where her in-laws had been interred, she wailed and wept in the open wilds.

sentences.zh: 忽一丈夫至，則清所授徒也，為指示，收二骸以歸。

translations.literal: Suddenly a man arrived — one of Qing's pupils — and showed her the way; she gathered both sets of remains and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a man arrived — one of Qing's pupils — and showed her the way. She gathered both sets of remains and returned home.

sentences.zh: 復冒暑之汴，負夫骨還。

translations.literal: Again braving the summer heat she went to Bianliang and brought back her husband's bones.
translations.idiomatic: Again braving the summer heat she went to Bianliang and brought back her husband's bones.

sentences.zh: 三喪畢舉，忍餓無他誌。

translations.literal: When all three funerals were complete, she endured hunger and held no other ambition.
translations.idiomatic: When all three funerals were complete, she endured hunger and held no other ambition.

sentences.zh: 學正劉崧言於知州馬暾，贖其女，厚恤之。

translations.literal: District Confucian director Liu Song spoke to prefect Ma Tun, who redeemed her daughter and gave her generous relief.
translations.idiomatic: District Confucian director Liu Song spoke to prefect Ma Tun, who redeemed her daughter and gave her generous relief.

sentences.zh: 年七十五乃卒。

translations.literal: She lived to seventy-five before she died.
translations.idiomatic: She lived to seventy-five before she died.

sentences.zh: 後有畢氏，河間鄧節妻。

translations.literal: Later there was Lady Bi, wife of Deng Jie of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Lady Bi, wife of Deng Jie of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 年饑，攜家景州就食，舅姑相繼亡，節亦尋歿，俱槁葬景州。

translations.literal: During a famine year she took her family to Jingzhou to seek food. Her husband's parents died in succession, and Jie soon followed; all were given rough burials in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year she took her family to Jingzhou to seek food. Her husband's parents died in succession, and Jie soon followed. All were given rough burials in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 氏年三十三，無子女，獨歸里中，忍饑凍，晝夜紡織，積數年，市地城北八里莊，獨之景州，負舅姑及夫骨還葬。

translations.literal: She was thirty-three, without children. Alone she returned to her hometown, enduring hunger and cold, spinning and weaving day and night. After several years she purchased land at Bali Village north of the city, traveled alone to Jingzhou, and carried back the bones of her in-laws and husband for reburial.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirty-three and without children. Alone she returned to her hometown, enduring hunger and cold while spinning and weaving day and night. After several years she purchased land at Bali Village north of the city, traveled alone to Jingzhou, and carried back the bones of her in-laws and husband for reburial.

sentences.zh: 石孝女，新昌人。

translations.literal: Shi the Filial Daughter was a native of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi the Filial Daughter was a native of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 繈褓時，父潛坐事籍沒，系京獄。

translations.literal: While still in swaddling clothes, her father Yin was implicated in a covert matter and his household was confiscated; he was imprisoned in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While still in swaddling clothes, her father Yin was implicated in a covert matter and his household was confiscated. He was imprisoned in the capital.

sentences.zh: 母吳以漏籍獲免，依兄弟為生。

translations.literal: Her mother Wu escaped punishment through an omission in the registry and relied on her brothers to live.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Wu escaped punishment through an omission in the registry and relied on her brothers to live.

sentences.zh: 一日，父脫歸，匿吳家。

translations.literal: One day her father escaped and returned, hiding in the Wu household.
translations.idiomatic: One day her father escaped and returned, hiding in the Wu household.

sentences.zh: 吳兄弟懼連坐，殺置大窖中，母不敢言。

translations.literal: Wu's brothers, fearing implication, killed him and disposed of his body in a great pit; the mother dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's brothers, fearing implication, killed him and disposed of his body in a great pit. The mother dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 及女長，問母曰：「我無父族何也？

translations.literal: When the daughter grew up she asked her mother: "Why have I no father's kin?
translations.idiomatic: When the daughter grew up she asked her mother, "Why have I no father's kin?

sentences.zh: 」母告之故，女大悲憤。

translations.literal: " Her mother told her the reason, and the daughter was stricken with great grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: " Her mother told her the reason, and the daughter was stricken with great grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，年十六，舅氏主婚配族子。

translations.literal: In the early Yongle period, at sixteen, her maternal uncle arranged her marriage to a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongle period, at sixteen, her maternal uncle arranged her marriage to a clansman.

sentences.zh: 女白母曰：「殺我父者，吳也。

translations.literal: The daughter told her mother: "Those who killed my father are the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter told her mother, "Those who killed my father are the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 奈何為父仇婦？

translations.literal: How can I become the wife of my father's killers?
translations.idiomatic: How can I become the wife of my father's killers?

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「事非我主，奈何？

translations.literal: " Her mother said: "The matter was not my decision — what could I do?
translations.idiomatic: " Her mother said, "The matter was not my decision — what could I do?

sentences.zh: 」女頷而不答。

translations.literal: " The daughter nodded but gave no answer.
translations.idiomatic: " The daughter nodded but gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 嫁之日，方禮賓，女自經室中。

translations.literal: On the day of the marriage, while receiving guests in ceremony, the daughter hanged herself in her room.
translations.idiomatic: On her wedding day, even as she was receiving guests in ceremony, the daughter hanged herself in her chamber.

sentences.zh: 母仰天哭曰：「吾女之死，不欲為仇人婦也。

translations.literal: Her mother looked up to heaven and wept, saying: "My daughter's death — she did not wish to become the wife of her enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother looked up to heaven and wept, saying, "My daughter died because she would not become the wife of her enemies.

sentences.zh: 」號慟數日亦死。

translations.literal: " She wailed in grief for several days and also died.
translations.idiomatic: " She wailed in grief for several days and then died as well.

sentences.zh: 有司聞之，治殺潛者罪。

translations.literal: When officials heard of it, they prosecuted those who had killed Yin.
translations.idiomatic: When officials learned of the affair, they prosecuted those who had killed Yin.

sentences.zh: 湯慧信，上海人。

translations.literal: Tang Huixin was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Huixin was a native of Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 通《孝經》、《列女傳》，嫁華亭鄧林。

translations.literal: She mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women, and married Deng Lin of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: She had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women, and married Deng Lin of Huating.

sentences.zh: 林卒，婦年二十五，一女七歲。

translations.literal: Lin died; the wife was twenty-five, with a daughter of seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died, his wife was twenty-five and they had a daughter of seven.

sentences.zh: 鄧族利其居，迫使歸家，婦曰：「我鄧家婦，何歸乎？

translations.literal: The Deng clan coveted her dwelling and forced her to return home. The wife said: "I am a wife of the Deng household — why should I return?
translations.idiomatic: The Deng clan coveted her home and tried to force her back to her natal family. The wife said, "I am a wife of the Deng household — why should I leave?

sentences.zh: 」族知不可奪，貿其居於巨室。

translations.literal: " The clan, knowing she could not be compelled, sold her dwelling to a great household.
translations.idiomatic: " Finding they could not force her, the clan sold her home to a wealthy family.

sentences.zh: 婦泣曰：「我收夫骨於茲土，與同存亡，奈何棄之。

translations.literal: The wife wept and said: "I gathered my husband's bones on this ground; I share life and death with them — how can I abandon them?
translations.idiomatic: The wife wept and said, "I gathered my husband's bones on this soil; I have pledged to live and die here — how can I abandon this place?

sentences.zh: 」欲自盡，巨室義而去之。

translations.literal: " She wished to kill herself; the great household, moved by righteousness, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " She was ready to take her own life; moved by her integrity, the wealthy family withdrew the purchase.

sentences.zh: 婦尋自計曰：「族利我財耳。

translations.literal: The wife soon reasoned to herself: "The clan covets my property, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The wife soon reasoned to herself, "The clan wants nothing but my property.

sentences.zh: 」乃出家資，盡畀族人，躬績纴以給。

translations.literal: " She then brought out her household assets and gave them all to the clan members, supporting herself by spinning and weaving in person.
translations.idiomatic: " She then brought out her household assets and gave them all to the clan, supporting herself by spinning and weaving with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 歲大水，居荒野沮洳中。

translations.literal: In a year of great flood she lived in the wild marshlands.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of great flood she lived in the wild marshlands.

sentences.zh: 其女適人者，操舟來迎，不許。

translations.literal: Her married daughter came by boat to welcome her; she would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Her married daughter came by boat to take her in, but she would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 請暫憩舟中，亦不許，曰：「我守此六十年，因巨浸以從汝父，所甘心焉，復何往！

translations.literal: When asked to rest briefly in the boat, she still refused, saying: "I have kept vigil here for sixty years; to follow your father in the great inundation is what my heart accepts — whither else would I go!
translations.idiomatic: When asked to rest briefly in the boat, she still refused, saying, "I have kept watch here for sixty years. To follow your father in the great flood is what my heart accepts — where else would I go?

sentences.zh: 」母女方相牽未舍，水至，湯竟溺死。

translations.literal: " Mother and daughter still held each other, unwilling to part; the water came, and Tang ultimately drowned.
translations.idiomatic: " Mother and daughter still clung to each other, unwilling to part. The floodwaters rose, and Tang drowned.

sentences.zh: 義婢妙聰，保安右衛指揮張孟喆家婢也。

translations.literal: Righteous maid Miao Cong was a servant in the household of Zhang Mengzhe, commander of the Bao'an Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous maid Miao Cong was a servant in the household of Zhang Mengzhe, commander of the Bao'an Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，調兵操宣府。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, troops were mobilized for drilling at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, troops were mobilized for training at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 孟喆在行。

translations.literal: Mengzhe was on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhe was away on campaign.

sentences.zh: 北寇入掠，妻李謂夫妹曰：「我命婦，與若皆宦門女，義不可辱。

translations.literal: Northern raiders entered to plunder. His wife Li said to his younger sister: "I am a wife bound by fate; you and I are both daughters of official households — righteousness forbids disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Northern raiders swept in to plunder. His wife Li said to his younger sister, "I am a wife bound by fate, and you and I are both daughters of official families — we cannot suffer disgrace.

sentences.zh: 」相挈投井中，妙聰亦隨入，見二人俱未死，以李有娠，恐水冷有所害，遂負之於背。

translations.literal: " Taking each other by the hand they threw themselves into a well; Miao Cong also followed them in. Seeing that both had not died — and because Li was pregnant, fearing the cold water might harm her — she bore Li on her back.
translations.idiomatic: " Hand in hand they threw themselves into a well; Miao Cong followed them in. Finding that both women were still alive — and because Li was pregnant, fearing the cold water might harm the child — she bore Li on her back.

sentences.zh: 賊退，孟喆弟仲喆求三人井中，以索引嫂妹出，而婢則死矣。

translations.literal: When the raiders withdrew, Mengzhe's younger brother Zhongzhe sought the three in the well and drew out his sister-in-law and sister by rope; the maid was dead.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew, Mengzhe's younger brother Zhongzhe found the three in the well and pulled his sister-in-law and sister out with a rope; the maid was dead.

sentences.zh: 徐孝女，嘉善徐遠女也。

translations.literal: Xu the Filial Daughter was the daughter of Xu Yuan of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu the Filial Daughter was the daughter of Xu Yuan of Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，母患臁瘡。

translations.literal: At six years of age, her mother suffered from leg ulcers.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six, her mother suffered from leg ulcers.

sentences.zh: 女問母何以得愈，母謾曰：「兒吮之乃愈。

translations.literal: The girl asked her mother how she could be cured; the mother said offhand: "If my child suckles them, they will heal.
translations.idiomatic: The girl asked her mother how the sores could be cured; the mother said offhand, "If my child suckles them, they will heal.

sentences.zh: 」女遂請吮，母難之。

translations.literal: " The girl then asked to suckle; the mother found it hard to allow it.
translations.idiomatic: " The girl then asked to suckle the wounds; her mother was reluctant to allow it.

sentences.zh: 女悲啼不已，母不得已聽之，吮數日，果愈。

translations.literal: The girl wept in grief without cease; the mother had no choice but to assent. After suckling for several days, the ulcers indeed healed.
translations.idiomatic: The girl wept without cease; at last the mother yielded. After several days of suckling, the ulcers indeed healed.

sentences.zh: 高氏女，武邑人，適諸生陳和。

translations.literal: A woman of the Gao clan, native of Wuyi, married the licentiate Chen He.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Gao clan, a native of Wuyi, married the licentiate Chen He.

sentences.zh: 和早卒，高獨持門戶，奉翁姑甚孝。

translations.literal: He died early; Gao alone kept the household gates and served her parents-in-law with great filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He died young; Gao alone kept the household and served her parents-in-law with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及宣德時，翁姑並歿，氏以禮殯葬，時年五十矣。

translations.literal: In the Xuande period her parents-in-law both died; the lady buried them according to ritual. She was then fifty.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign her parents-in-law both died; she buried them according to ritual. She was then fifty.

sentences.zh: 泣謂子剛曰：「我父，洪武間舉家客河南虞城。

translations.literal: Weeping she said to her son Gang: "My father, in the Hongwu period, took the whole family as guests to Yucheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she said to her son Gang, "In the Hongwu period my father took our whole family to live as guests in Yucheng, Henan.

sentences.zh: 父死，旋葬城北，母以刺木小車輞識之。

translations.literal: When he died he was soon buried north of the city; my mother marked the spot with a small cart wheel-rim of carved wood.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was buried north of the city; my mother marked the grave with a small wooden cart-wheel rim.

sentences.zh: 比還家，母亦死，弟懦不能自振。

translations.literal: By the time we returned home, my mother had also died; my younger brother was timid and could not sustain himself.
translations.idiomatic: By the time we returned home, my mother had also died. My younger brother was timid and could not support himself.

sentences.zh: 吾三十年不敢言者，以汝王母在堂，當朝夕侍養也。

translations.literal: I have for thirty years not dared speak of this, because your paternal grandmother was still alive and I had to attend her morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years I did not dare speak of this, because your grandmother was still alive and I had to attend her day and night.

sentences.zh: 今大事已畢，欲舁吾父遺骸歸合葬。

translations.literal: Now the great affairs are complete; I wish to raise my father's remains and return them for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the great obligations are fulfilled, I wish to exhume my father's remains and bring them home for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 」剛唯唯，隨母至虞城，抵葬所，冢累累不能辨。

translations.literal: " Gang assented; he followed his mother to Yucheng and reached the burial grounds, but mounds lay one upon another and could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: " Gang assented and followed his mother to Yucheng. At the burial grounds mounds lay one upon another and none could be identified.

sentences.zh: 氏以發系馬鞍逆行，自朝及夕，至一小冢，鞍重不能前，即開其冢，所識車輞宛然。

translations.literal: The lady tied her hair to a saddle and walked against the direction of the horse from morning till evening. At a small mound the saddle grew heavy and could not advance; she opened the tomb, and the recognizable wheel-rim was indeed there.
translations.idiomatic: The lady tied her hair to a saddle and walked against the horse's direction from morning till evening. At one small mound the saddle suddenly grew heavy and the horse would not advance; she opened the tomb, and the familiar wheel-rim was there.

sentences.zh: 遠近觀者鹹驚異，助之歸，啟母窆同葬。

translations.literal: Onlookers near and far were all astonished; they helped her return, opened her mother's crypt, and buried them together.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers near and far were astonished. They helped her return home, opened her mother's tomb, and buried the couple together.

sentences.zh: 孫義婦，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Sun the Chaste Wife was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun the Chaste Wife was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 歸定海黃誼昭，生子湑。

translations.literal: She married Huang Yizhao of Dinghai and bore a son, Xu.
translations.idiomatic: She married Huang Yizhao of Dinghai and bore a son named Xu.

sentences.zh: 未幾夫卒，孫育之成立，求兄女為配。

translations.literal: Before long her husband died; Sun raised him to maturity and sought her elder brother's daughter as a match.
translations.idiomatic: Before long her husband died. Sun raised the boy to maturity and found a wife for him in her elder brother's daughter.

sentences.zh: 甫三年，生二子，湑亦卒。

translations.literal: After only three years two sons were born, and Xu also died.
translations.idiomatic: After only three years two sons were born, and then Xu also died.

sentences.zh: 時田賦皆令民自輸，孫姑婦相率攜幼子輸賦南京，訴尚書蹇義，言：「縣苦潮患，十年九荒，乞築海塘障之。

translations.literal: At the time land tax was all required to be delivered by the people themselves. Sun and her daughter-in-law together took their young sons to deliver tax at Nanjing, petitioning the Minister Jian Yi, saying: "The county suffers grievously from tidal inundation — nine years of famine in ten. We beg that a sea dyke be built to ward it off.
translations.idiomatic: At that time land tax had to be delivered in person. Sun and her daughter-in-law together took their young sons to pay tax in Nanjing and petitioned Minister Jian Yi, saying, "Our county suffers terribly from tidal floods — nine years of famine in ten. We beg that a sea dyke be built to hold them back.

sentences.zh: 」義見其孤苦，詰曰：「何為不嫁？

translations.literal: " Yi saw their destitution and questioned them: "Why do you not remarry?
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing their destitution, Yi asked, "Why do you not remarry?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「餓死事極小，失節事極大。

translations.literal: " They replied: "To starve is a very small matter; to lose chastity is a very great one.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "Starving is a very small matter; losing one's chastity is a very great one.

sentences.zh: 」義嗟嘆久之，次日即為奏請，遣官偕有司相度成之，起自龍山，迄於觀海，永免潮患。

translations.literal: " Yi sighed in admiration for a long time; the next day he at once memorialized the throne, dispatched officials together with local authorities to survey and complete it, running from Longshan to Guanhai — forever freeing them from tidal calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi sighed in admiration for a long while. The next day he memorialized the throne at once, sent officials with local authorities to survey the site and complete the work, from Longshan to Guanhai — forever freeing the county from tidal disaster.

sentences.zh: 慈谿人廟祀之塘上。

translations.literal: The people of Cixi built a shrine to worship her on the dyke.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cixi built a shrine to her on the dyke.

sentences.zh: 梁氏，大城尹之路妻。

translations.literal: Lady Liang was the wife of Yin Zhilu of Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang was the wife of Yin Zhilu of Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 嫁歲餘，夫乏食出遊山海關，賣熟食為生。

translations.literal: After a year of marriage her husband, lacking food, went to roam at Shanhai Pass and sold prepared food to live.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year of marriage, her husband, lacking food, went to Shanhai Pass and sold prepared food to make a living.

sentences.zh: 又娶馬氏，生子二，十余年不通問。

translations.literal: He took another wife, surnamed Ma, who bore two sons; for more than ten years no word passed between them.
translations.idiomatic: There he took another wife, surnamed Ma, who bore two sons. For more than ten years no word passed between them.

sentences.zh: 氏事翁姑，艱苦無怨言。

translations.literal: The lady served her parents-in-law through hardship without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang served her parents-in-law through hardship without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 夫客死，氏徒步行乞，迎夫喪，往返二千里，迄扶柩攜後妻二子以歸，裏人嘆異。

translations.literal: When her husband died abroad, the lady walked on foot begging alms to receive his coffin — two thousand li there and back — and at last escorted the bier and brought back the later wife and two sons; neighbors marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died abroad, she walked on foot, begging alms to fetch his coffin — two thousand li there and back — and at last escorted the bier home with his second wife and two sons. Her neighbors marvelled.

sentences.zh: 余佈妻馬氏，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Ma, wife of Yu Bu, was a native of Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Ma, wife of Yu Bu, was a native of Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 歸五年，夫死無子，家酷貧。

translations.literal: Five years after marriage her husband died without sons; the household was desperately poor.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after her marriage her husband died without sons, and the household was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 姑欲奪其誌，有田二畝半，得粟不以與婦，馬不為動。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law wished to force her to abandon her resolve. There were two and a half mou of fields; the grain obtained was not given to the wife — Ma was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law tried to force her to abandon her vow of widowhood. The family had two and a half mou of fields, but the grain harvested was withheld from her — Ma remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 姑潛納他人聘，一夕鼓吹臨門，趣治妝，馬入臥室自經死，幾上食器，糠乞尚存。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law secretly accepted another's betrothal gift; one evening music and drums came to the gate, urging her to prepare her bridal dress. Ma entered the bedroom and hanged herself. On the table food vessels still held the bran she had begged.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law secretly accepted another man's betrothal gift. One evening music and drums came to the gate, urging her to prepare her bridal dress. Ma went to the bedroom and hanged herself. On the table her bowl still held the bran she had begged.

sentences.zh: 義姑萬氏，名義顓，字祖心，鄞人，寧波衛指揮僉事鐘女也。

translations.literal: Righteous aunt Wan, personal name Yizhuan, courtesy name Zuxin, native of Yin, daughter of Zhong, assistant commander of the Ningbo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous aunt Wan, personal name Yizhuan, courtesy name Zuxin, a native of Yin, was the daughter of Zhong, assistant commander of the Ningbo Guard.

sentences.zh: 幼貞靜，善讀書。

translations.literal: From youth she was chaste and quiet, skilled at reading.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was chaste and quiet, and skilled at reading.

sentences.zh: 兩兄文、武，皆襲世職，戰死，旁無期功之親。

translations.literal: Her two elder brothers Wen and Wu both inherited hereditary posts and died in battle; there were no close collateral relatives at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Her two elder brothers Wen and Wu both inherited hereditary posts and died in battle, leaving no close collateral relatives.

sentences.zh: 繼母曹氏，兩嫂陳氏、吳氏，皆盛年孀居。

translations.literal: Her stepmother Lady Cao and two sisters-in-law, the Ladies Chen and Wu, all widowed in the prime of life.
translations.idiomatic: Her stepmother Lady Cao and her two sisters-in-law, the Ladies Chen and Wu, were all widowed in the prime of life.

sentences.zh: 吳遺腹僅六月，姑旦暮拜天哭告曰：「萬氏絕矣，願天賜一男，續忠臣後。

translations.literal: Wu's posthumous child was only six months; the aunt morning and evening bowed to Heaven weeping and praying: "The Wan line is cut off — may Heaven grant a son to continue the loyal minister's line.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu's posthumous child was only six months along. Morning and evening the aunt bowed to Heaven, weeping and praying, "The Wan line is cut off — may Heaven grant a son to carry on the loyal minister's line.

sentences.zh: 我矢不嫁，共撫之。

translations.literal: I vow not to marry; together we shall raise him.
translations.idiomatic: I swear I will not marry; together we shall raise him.

sentences.zh: 」已果生男，名之曰全。

translations.literal: " Before long a son was indeed born; they named him Quan.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long a son was indeed born, and they named him Quan.

sentences.zh: 姑喜曰：「萬氏有後矣。

translations.literal: The aunt rejoiced and said: "The Wan line has an heir now.
translations.idiomatic: The aunt rejoiced and said, "The Wan line has an heir now.

sentences.zh: 」乃與諸嫠共守，名閥來聘，皆謝絕之，訓全讀書，迄底成立。

translations.literal: " She then with the other widows together kept vigil; eminent families came with marriage proposals — all were declined. They trained Quan in reading until he reached full maturity.
translations.idiomatic: " She then joined the other widows in keeping the household. Eminent families sent marriage proposals — all were declined. They trained Quan in letters until he came of age.

sentences.zh: 全嗣職，傳子禧、孫椿，皆奉姑訓惟謹。

translations.literal: Quan succeeded to the post; his sons Xi and grandson Chun all followed the aunt's instruction with scrupulous care.
translations.idiomatic: Quan succeeded to the hereditary post; his son Xi and grandson Chun all obeyed the aunt's instruction with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 姑年七十余卒。

translations.literal: The aunt died in her seventies.
translations.idiomatic: The aunt died in her seventies.

sentences.zh: 姑之祖斌及父兄並死王事，母及二嫂守貞數十年，姑更以義著。

translations.literal: The aunt's grandfather Bin and her father and brothers all died in the king's service; her mother and two sisters-in-law kept chastity for decades; the aunt was still further distinguished for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The aunt's grandfather Bin, her father, and her brothers had all died in the king's service; her mother and two sisters-in-law kept chastity for decades; the aunt was still further distinguished for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 鄉人重之，稱為四忠三節一義之門。

translations.literal: The villagers held them in esteem, calling them the gate of four loyal ministers, three chaste widows, and one woman of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers held them in high esteem, calling their household the gate of four loyal ministers, three chaste widows, and one woman of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 後有陳義姑者，沙縣陳穗女。

translations.literal: Later there was Chen the Righteous Aunt, daughter of Chen Sui of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Chen the Righteous Aunt, daughter of Chen Sui of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 年十八，父母相繼卒，遺二男，長七歲，次五歲。

translations.literal: At eighteen her parents died in succession, leaving two sons — the elder seven, the younger five.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen her parents died in succession, leaving two younger brothers — the elder seven, the younger five.

sentences.zh: 親族利其有，日眈眈於旁。

translations.literal: Relatives coveted their property and day by day watched them with greedy eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives coveted their property and watched them day and night with greedy eyes.

sentences.zh: 姑矢誌撫弟，居常置帚數十。

translations.literal: The aunt vowed to raise her younger brothers and ordinarily kept several dozen brooms at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The aunt vowed to raise her brothers and kept several dozen brooms ready at all times.

sentences.zh: 族兄弟暮夜叩門，姑燃帚照之，亟啟戶具酒食款。

translations.literal: Clansmen came knocking at the door at night; the aunt lit a broom to illuminate them and at once opened the door and set out wine and food to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen knocked at the door at night, the aunt would light a broom to illuminate them, then open the door and set out wine and food to receive them.

sentences.zh: 叩者告曰：「吾輩夜行滅火，就求燭耳。

translations.literal: The callers said: "We were traveling at night with our lamps extinguished and came only to ask for a candle.
translations.idiomatic: The callers would say, "We were traveling at night with our lamps out and came only to ask for a light.

sentences.zh: 」自此窺伺者絕意。

translations.literal: " From then on those who had been watching for an opportunity gave up the idea.
translations.idiomatic: " After that, those who had been watching for an opportunity gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 及二弟畢婚，年四十五乃嫁，終無子。

translations.literal: When both younger brothers had completed their marriages, at forty-five she finally married; she had no children to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Only after both brothers had married did she marry herself, at forty-five. She had no children.

sentences.zh: 二弟迎歸，母事之。

translations.literal: Her two younger brothers welcomed her home and served her as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her two brothers welcomed her home and served her as they would a mother.

sentences.zh: 郭氏，大田人。

translations.literal: Lady Guo was a native of Datian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo was a native of Datian.

sentences.zh: 鄧茂七之亂，鄉人結寨東巖。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Deng Maoqi, the villagers built a stockade at East Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of Deng Maoqi, the villagers built a stockade at East Cliff.

sentences.zh: 寨破，郭褓幼兒走，且有身，為賊所驅。

translations.literal: When the stockade fell, Guo fled carrying an infant and was also pregnant; she was driven along by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the stockade fell, Guo fled with an infant in her arms; she was also pregnant and was driven along by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 郭奮罵，投百尺巖下，與兒俱碎亂石間，胎及腸胃迸出，狼籍巖下。

translations.literal: Guo cursed them fiercely and threw herself from a cliff a hundred feet high; she and the child were shattered among the rocks, the fetus and entrails bursting forth and strewn below the cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Guo cursed them fiercely and threw herself from a cliff a hundred feet high. She and the child were shattered on the rocks below; the fetus and her entrails burst forth and lay strewn at the foot of the cliff.

sentences.zh: 賊據高瞰之，皆嘆曰：「真烈婦也！

translations.literal: The bandits looked down from above and all sighed: "A truly heroic woman!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels looked down from above and sighed, "A truly heroic woman!

sentences.zh: 」瘞之去。

translations.literal: " They buried her and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " They buried her and departed.

sentences.zh: 同時有幼溪女，失其姓名。

translations.literal: At the same time there was a girl of Youxi whose name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was a girl of Youxi whose name is lost.

sentences.zh: 茂七破沙縣，匿草間，為二賊所獲。

translations.literal: When Maoqi took Shaxian she hid in the grass and was seized by two bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoqi captured Shaxian she hid in the grass and was seized by two rebels.

sentences.zh: 遇溪橋，貞女曰：「扶我過，當從一人而終。

translations.literal: Coming to a stream bridge, the chaste girl said: "Help me across, and I will follow one of you to the end.
translations.idiomatic: At a stream bridge the chaste girl said, "Help me across, and I will give myself to one of you forever.

sentences.zh: 」二賊爭趨挽，至橋半，女視溪流湍急，拽二賊投水中，俱溺死。

translations.literal: " The two bandits rushed forward vying to support her; halfway across the bridge the girl saw the stream rushing swiftly, seized both bandits and pulled them into the water — all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: " The two rebels rushed forward, each vying to support her. Halfway across the bridge she saw how swift the current was, seized both men, and pulled them into the water. All three drowned.

sentences.zh: 程氏，揚州胡尚絅妻。

translations.literal: Lady Cheng was the wife of Hu Shangjiong of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng was the wife of Hu Shangjiong of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚絅嬰危疾，婦刲腕肉啖之，不能咽而卒。

translations.literal: Shangjiong fell gravely ill; the wife cut flesh from her wrist and fed it to him, but he could not swallow it and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangjiong fell gravely ill, his wife cut flesh from her wrist and fed it to him, but he could not swallow it and died.

sentences.zh: 婦號慟不食二日。

translations.literal: The wife wailed in grief and ate nothing for two days.
translations.idiomatic: The wife wailed in grief and ate nothing for two days.

sentences.zh: 懷孕四月矣，或曰：「得男可延夫嗣，徒死何為？

translations.literal: She was four months pregnant; someone said: "If you bear a son you can continue your husband's line — what use is dying in vain?
translations.idiomatic: She was four months pregnant. Someone said, "If you bear a son you can continue your husband's line — why die for nothing?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「吾亦知之，倘生女，徒茍活數月耳。

translations.literal: " She replied: "I know that too; but if I bear a daughter, I would merely live on in shame for a few months.
translations.idiomatic: " She replied, "I know that — but if I bear a daughter, I would only drag out a shameful life for a few months.

sentences.zh: 」因復食，彌月果生男。

translations.literal: " She therefore ate again; after a full month a son was indeed born.
translations.idiomatic: " She therefore began to eat again. A month later she bore a son.

sentences.zh: 明年殤，即前語翁姑曰：「媳不能常侍奉，有娣姒在，無悲也。

translations.literal: The next year the child died in infancy; she then spoke beforehand to her parents-in-law: "Your daughter-in-law cannot attend you always; your younger sons' wives are here — do not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the child died in infancy. She then said to her parents-in-law, "I cannot attend you forever; your younger sons' wives are here — do not grieve.

sentences.zh: 」復絕食，越二日其姑撫之曰：「爾父母家二百里內，若不俟面訣乎？

translations.literal: " She again stopped eating. After two days her mother-in-law comforted her: "Your parents' home is within two hundred li — will you not wait to bid them farewell face to face?
translations.idiomatic: " She again stopped eating. After two days her mother-in-law comforted her, saying, "Your parents' home is within two hundred li — will you not wait to bid them farewell?

sentences.zh: 」婦曰：「可急迎之。

translations.literal: " The wife said: "Send for them at once.
translations.idiomatic: " The wife said, "Send for them at once.

sentences.zh: 」日飲米沈一匙以待。

translations.literal: " Each day she drank one spoonful of rice water and waited.
translations.idiomatic: " Each day she drank one spoonful of rice water and waited.

sentences.zh: 逾十有二日，父母遣幼弟至，婦曰：「是可白吾誌。

translations.literal: After more than twelve days her parents sent her younger brother; the wife said: "This will suffice to make my resolve known.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twelve days her parents sent her younger brother. The wife said, "This will suffice to make my resolve known.

sentences.zh: 」自是滴水不入口，徐簡中奩簪珥，令辦後事，以其余散家人並鄰嫗嘗通問者，復自卜曰：「十八、九日皆良，吾當逝。

translations.literal: " From then on she took not a drop of water. Slowly she sorted the hairpins and earrings in her dressing case, had her affairs put in order, distributed the remainder to her family and to neighboring old women who had once exchanged greetings with her, and divined for herself again, saying: "The eighteenth and nineteenth are both auspicious days — I shall depart.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on she refused all food and drink. She calmly sorted the hairpins and earrings in her dressing case, arranged her final affairs, gave what remained to her family and to neighboring women who had once called on her, and cast the lots again for herself, saying, "The eighteenth and nineteenth are both good days — I shall die then.

sentences.zh: 向曾刲肉救夫，夫不可救，以灰和之置床頭，附吾左腕，以示全歸。

translations.literal: Earlier I cut flesh to save my husband; he could not be saved. Mix it with ashes and place it at the head of the bed; attach it to my left wrist, to show complete return.
translations.idiomatic: I once cut flesh to save my husband, but he could not be saved. Mix it with ashes and place it at the head of the bed, and attach it to my left wrist — a token that I return to him whole.

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she died.
translations.idiomatic: " And so she died.

sentences.zh: 王妙鳳，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Miaofeng was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Miaofeng was from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 適吳奎。

translations.literal: She married Wu Kui.
translations.idiomatic: She was married to Wu Kui.

sentences.zh: 姑有淫行。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law had licentious conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was licentious.

sentences.zh: 正統中，奎商於外。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, Kui went away on business.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong era, Kui went away on business.

sentences.zh: 姑與所私飲，並欲汙之，命妙鳳取酒，挈瓶不進。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law drank with her paramour and also wished to defile her; she ordered Miaofeng to fetch wine, but Miaofeng took the bottle and would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law was drinking with her lover and wished to force Miaofeng as well; she ordered her to fetch wine, but Miaofeng took the bottle and refused to go in.

sentences.zh: 頻促之，不得已而入。

translations.literal: Urged repeatedly, she had no choice but to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again and again, she had no choice but to go in.

sentences.zh: 姑所私戲紾其臂。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law's paramour playfully twisted her arm.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law's lover playfully seized her arm.

sentences.zh: 妙鳳憤，拔刀斫臂不殊，再斫乃絕。

translations.literal: Miaofeng in fury drew a knife and hacked at her arm; the first blow did not sever it — only the second cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Miaofeng drew a knife and struck at her arm; the first blow failed to sever it, and only the second cut it clean off.

sentences.zh: 父母欲訟之官，妙鳳曰：「死則死耳，豈有婦訟姑理邪？

translations.literal: Her parents wished to bring suit before the magistrate; Miaofeng said: "Die, then die — how could there be reason for a daughter-in-law to sue her mother-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: Her parents wanted to take the matter to court. Miaofeng said, "If I must die, then let me die — what sense is there in a daughter-in-law bringing suit against her mother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 」逾旬卒。

translations.literal: " Within ten days she died.
translations.idiomatic: " Within ten days she was dead.

sentences.zh: 唐貴梅者，貴池人。

translations.literal: Tang Guimei was a native of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Guimei was from Guichi.

sentences.zh: 適同里朱姓。

translations.literal: She married a man of the Zhu clan in the same district.
translations.idiomatic: She married a man surnamed Zhu from the same district.

sentences.zh: 姑與富商私，見貴梅悅之，以金帛賄其姑，誨婦淫者，百端勿聽，加箠楚勿聽，繼以炮烙，終不聽。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law had an affair with a wealthy merchant; seeing that Guimei pleased him, he bribed the mother-in-law with gold and silks. The mother-in-law instructed the daughter-in-law in lewdness by every means — she would not listen; she beat her with rods and she would not listen; she applied burning torture, and still she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was carrying on with a wealthy merchant. When he took a liking to Guimei, he bribed the mother-in-law with gold and silk. The mother-in-law tried every persuasion to make the young wife submit — she refused; she beat her with rods — she refused; she even subjected her to burning torture, and still she refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以不孝訟於官。
