translations.literal: Thereupon she sued her at court on a charge of unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At last the mother-in-law sued her in court for unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 通判某受商賂，拷之幾死者數矣。

translations.literal: A certain assistant prefect accepted the merchant's bribe and tortured her nearly to death several times.
translations.idiomatic: A certain assistant prefect took the merchant's bribe and had her beaten nearly to death on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 商冀其改節，復令姑保出之。

translations.literal: The merchant hoped she would change her chaste resolve; he again had the mother-in-law bail her out.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant hoped she would abandon her resolve; he had the mother-in-law bail her out again.

sentences.zh: 親黨勸婦首實，婦曰：「若爾，妾之名幸全，如播姑之惡何？

translations.literal: Relatives urged the wife to confess the truth; the wife said: "If I did so, my own name might be preserved intact — but how could I broadcast my mother-in-law's wickedness?
translations.idiomatic: Kinsfolk urged her to tell the whole truth. The wife said, "If I did, my own name might remain unstained — but how could I expose my mother-in-law's shame?

sentences.zh: 」夜易服，自經後園梅樹下。

translations.literal: " At night she changed her clothes and hanged herself beneath a plum tree in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: " That night she changed her clothes and hanged herself from a plum tree in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 及旦姑起，且將撻之。

translations.literal: At dawn the mother-in-law rose and was about to beat her.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the mother-in-law got up, intending to beat her.

sentences.zh: 至園中乃知其死，屍懸樹三日，顏如生。

translations.literal: When she reached the garden she learned of her death; the corpse hung from the tree for three days, her face still as in life.
translations.idiomatic: When she went into the garden she found her dead. The body hung from the tree for three days, her face still lifelike.

sentences.zh: 其後，嘉靖二十三年，有嘉定張氏者，嫁汪客之子。

translations.literal: Later, in the twenty-third year of Jiajing, there was a woman of the Zhang clan of Jiading who married the son of a man surnamed Wang, a guest laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign, a woman of the Zhang clan of Jiading married the son of a migrant worker surnamed Wang.

sentences.zh: 其姑多與人私，諸惡少中有胡巖者，最桀黠，群黨皆聽其指使。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law had many illicit affairs; among the local ruffians one Hu Yan was the fiercest and most cunning, and the whole gang obeyed his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law kept many lovers. Among the local ruffians, one Hu Yan was the boldest and most cunning, and the whole gang did his bidding.

sentences.zh: 於是與姑謀，遣其子入縣為卒，而巖等日夕縱飲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he plotted with the mother-in-law to send her son into the county town as a soldier, while Yan and his fellows drank day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with the mother-in-law to send her son into the county town as a conscript, while Yan and his companions caroused day and night.

sentences.zh: 一日，呼婦共坐，不應。

translations.literal: One day they called the wife to sit with them; she would not.
translations.idiomatic: One day they summoned the wife to sit with them; she refused.

sentences.zh: 巖從後攫其梳，婦折梳擲地。

translations.literal: Yan snatched her comb from behind; the wife broke the comb and threw it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yan grabbed her comb from behind; she snapped it and threw it to the floor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，巖徑入犯婦。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yan went straight in and violated the wife.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yan went in and assaulted her.

sentences.zh: 婦大呼殺人，以杵擊巖。

translations.literal: The wife cried out that someone was killing her and struck Yan with a pestle.
translations.idiomatic: She screamed that she was being murdered and struck Yan with a pestle.

sentences.zh: 巖怒走出，婦自投於地，哭終夜不絕，氣息僅屬。

translations.literal: Yan stormed out in anger; the wife threw herself to the ground and wept all night without cease, her breath barely remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fled in a rage. The wife collapsed to the ground and wept all night without stopping, barely clinging to life.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，巖與姑恐事泄，縶諸床足守之。

translations.literal: At dawn Yan and the mother-in-law, fearing the affair would leak out, bound her to the bedposts and kept watch over her.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, fearing exposure, Yan and the mother-in-law tied her to the bedposts and stood guard.

sentences.zh: 明日召諸惡少酣飲。

translations.literal: The next day they summoned the ruffians for a drunken revel.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they called the ruffians together for a drinking bout.

sentences.zh: 二鼓共縛婦，槌斧交下。

translations.literal: At the second watch they bound the wife together and rained down mallets and axes upon her.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch they bound her fast and beat her with mallets and axes.

sentences.zh: 婦痛苦宛轉曰：「何不以利刃刺我。

translations.literal: The wife in agony writhed and said: "Why not use a sharp blade to stab me?
translations.idiomatic: Writhing in pain, the wife cried, "Why not stab me with a sharp blade?

sentences.zh: 」一人乃前刺其頸，一人刺其脅，又椓其陰。

translations.literal: " One man then stabbed her in the neck, one stabbed her in the side, and another struck her private parts.
translations.idiomatic: " One man stabbed her in the neck, another in the ribs, and a third struck her in the groin.

sentences.zh: 舉屍欲焚之，屍重不可舉，乃火其室。

translations.literal: They tried to lift the corpse to burn it, but the body was too heavy to lift; thereupon they set fire to the house.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to lift the corpse to burn it, but the body was too heavy to move, so they set the house ablaze.

sentences.zh: 鄰裏救火者蹋門入，見嚇然死人，驚聞於官。

translations.literal: Neighbors fighting the fire kicked in the door and entered; seeing the startling corpse of the dead woman, they reported it in alarm to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors fighting the fire broke down the door and found the ghastly corpse; horrified, they reported it to the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 官逮小女奴及諸惡少鞫之，具得其實，皆以次受刑。

translations.literal: The magistrate arrested the young maidservant and the ruffians and interrogated them; the full truth was obtained, and each in turn received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate arrested the young maidservant and the ruffians and questioned them. The whole truth came out, and each was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 婦死時年十九。

translations.literal: When the wife died she was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: The wife was nineteen when she died.

sentences.zh: 邑故有烈婦祠，婦死前三日，祠旁人聞空中鼓樂聲，火炎炎從祠柱中出，人以為貞婦死事之征雲。

translations.literal: The district had long had a shrine to chaste women; three days before the wife's death, people beside the shrine heard drum and pipe music in the air, and flames blazed forth from the shrine pillars — men took this as a sign of the chaste woman's death.
translations.idiomatic: The district had long maintained a shrine to chaste women. Three days before her death, people near the shrine heard music in the air and saw flames burst from its pillars — taken as an omen of the chaste wife's martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 楊泰奴，仁和楊得安女。

translations.literal: Yang Tainu was the daughter of Yang Dean of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tainu was the daughter of Yang Dean of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 許嫁未行。

translations.literal: She was betrothed but the marriage had not yet taken place.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed, though the wedding had not yet been held.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，母疫病不愈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun her mother fell ill with an epidemic disease and did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun her mother fell gravely ill with an epidemic and could not recover.

sentences.zh: 泰奴三割胸肉食母，不效。

translations.literal: Tainu three times cut flesh from her breast to feed her mother; it had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Three times Tainu cut flesh from her breast to feed her mother, but to no avail.

sentences.zh: 一日薄幕，剖胸取肝一片，昏仆良久。

translations.literal: One day at dusk she cut open her breast and took out a piece of liver; she collapsed in a faint for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: One evening at dusk she cut open her breast and took out a piece of liver, then collapsed in a faint for a long while.

sentences.zh: 及蘇，以衣裹創，手和粥以進，母遂愈。

translations.literal: When she revived she wrapped the wound in cloth, mixed porridge with her hands, and presented it; her mother then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When she came to, she bound the wound with cloth, mixed porridge with her own hands, and fed it to her mother, who then recovered.

sentences.zh: 母宿有膝攣疾，亦愈。

translations.literal: Her mother had long suffered from a knee-contraction ailment; that too was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother had long suffered from a crippling knee ailment; that too was cured.

sentences.zh: 後有張氏，儀真周祥妻。

translations.literal: Later there was a Lady Zhang, wife of Zhou Xiang of Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was a Lady Zhang, wife of Zhou Xiang of Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 姑病，醫百方不效。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law fell ill; a hundred medical prescriptions had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law fell ill, and a hundred remedies failed.

sentences.zh: 一方士至其門曰：「人肝可療。

translations.literal: A Daoist adept came to their door and said: "Human liver can cure it.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist adept came to their door and said, "Human liver can cure it.

sentences.zh: 」張割左脅下，得膜如絮，以手探之沒腕，取肝二寸許，無少痛，作羹以進姑，病遂瘳。

translations.literal: " Zhang cut beneath her left side, obtained a membrane like cotton fluff; probing with her hand it went in to the wrist; she took out liver about two inches long, without the slightest pain, made broth and presented it to her mother-in-law, and the illness was then cured.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang cut beneath her left ribs, found a membrane like cotton fluff, and reached in until her hand sank to the wrist. She took out a piece of liver about two inches long without feeling any pain, cooked it into a broth for her mother-in-law, and the illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 陳氏，祥符人。

translations.literal: Lady Chen was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 字楊瑄，未嫁而瑄卒。

translations.literal: She was betrothed to Yang Xuan; before the marriage Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Yang Xuan, but before the wedding Xuan died.

sentences.zh: 女請死，父母不許，欲往哭，又不許。

translations.literal: The girl asked to die; her parents would not permit it. She wished to go and mourn, and again they would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The girl begged to die; her parents refused. She wished to go and mourn him, and they refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 私剪發，屬媒氏置瑄懷。

translations.literal: In secret she cut off her hair and entrusted it to the matchmaker to place in Xuan's bosom.
translations.idiomatic: In secret she cut off her hair and had the matchmaker place it in Xuan's coffin.

sentences.zh: 汴俗聘女，以金書生年月日畀男家，號定婚帖。

translations.literal: The custom of Bian when betrothing a daughter was to give the man's family a slip on which her birth year, month, and day were written in gold — called the betrothal contract.
translations.idiomatic: In Bian it was the custom, when betrothing a daughter, to give the groom's family a slip recording her birth date in gold ink — the betrothal contract.

sentences.zh: 瑄母乃以帖裹其發，置瑄懷以葬。

translations.literal: Xuan's mother then wrapped the contract around her hair and placed it in Xuan's bosom for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's mother wrapped the contract around the hair and placed both in Xuan's coffin for burial.

sentences.zh: 女遂素服以居。

translations.literal: The girl then lived in plain white mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: The girl thereafter lived in plain white mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 亡何，父母謀改聘，女縊死。

translations.literal: Before long her parents plotted to betroth her elsewhere; the girl hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long her parents planned to marry her to someone else; she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 後五十三年，至正德中，瑄侄永康改葬瑄，求陳骨合焉。

translations.literal: Fifty-three years later, in the Zhengde reign, Xuan's nephew Yongkang reburied Xuan and sought Chen's bones to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-three years later, during the Zhengde reign, Xuan's nephew Yongkang reburied him and sought Lady Chen's remains to join with his.

sentences.zh: 二骨朽矣，發及定婚帖鮮完如故。

translations.literal: Both sets of bones had decayed, but the hair and the betrothal contract were still perfectly intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: Both skeletons had crumbled to dust, but the hair and betrothal contract were still perfectly preserved.

sentences.zh: 葬三年，岐谷、丫瓜產墓上。

translations.literal: Three years after the burial, twin gourds and bottle gourds sprouted on the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after the burial, twin gourds sprouted on the tomb.

sentences.zh: 張氏，秀水人。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 年十四，受同邑諸生劉伯春聘。

translations.literal: At fourteen she received betrothal from Liu Bochun, a student of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she was betrothed to Liu Bochun, a student from the same district.

sentences.zh: 伯春負才名，必欲舉於鄉而後娶。

translations.literal: Bochun carried a reputation for talent and insisted on passing the provincial examination before marrying.
translations.idiomatic: Bochun had a reputation for literary talent and insisted on passing the provincial examination before they wed.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，女號泣絕發，自為詩祭之。

translations.literal: Before long he died; the girl wailed until her hair fell out and composed a poem herself to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died. The girl wept until her hair fell out and wrote a poem of mourning for him herself.

sentences.zh: 持服三年，不逾閫，不茹葷。

translations.literal: She observed mourning for three years, never crossing the threshold, never eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: She mourned for three years without crossing the threshold or eating meat.

sentences.zh: 服闋，即絕飲食，父母強諭之，終不食，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended she at once stopped eating and drinking; her parents urged her forcefully, yet she would not eat, and within ten days she died.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended she stopped eating and drinking altogether. Her parents pleaded with her, but she would not eat, and within ten days she was dead.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舅姑迎柩合葬焉。

translations.literal: She was twenty years old; her parents-in-law welcomed the coffin and buried her with him in a joint grave.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty. Her parents-in-law received her coffin and buried her beside him in a joint grave.

sentences.zh: 又有江夏歐陽金貞者，父梧，授《孝經》、《列女傳》。

translations.literal: There was also Ouyang Jinzhen of Jiangxia; her father Wu taught her the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ouyang Jinzhen of Jiangxia. Her father Wu taught her the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 稍長，字羅欽仰，從梧之官柘城。

translations.literal: When she was somewhat grown she was betrothed to Luo Qinyang and followed Wu to his post at Zhecheng.
translations.idiomatic: When she was older she was betrothed to Luo Qinyang and accompanied her father to his post at Zhecheng.

sentences.zh: 梧艱歸，舟次儀真，欽仰墜水死。

translations.literal: Wu encountered mourning and returned; the boat stopped at Yizhen, and Qinyang fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu entered mourning and returned home, the boat stopped at Yizhen; Qinyang fell into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 金貞年甫十四，驚哭欲赴水從之，父母持不許。

translations.literal: Jinzhen was just fourteen; startled, she wept and wished to throw herself into the water to follow him, but her parents held her back and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhen was only fourteen. Weeping in shock, she tried to throw herself into the water after him, but her parents held her back.

sentences.zh: 又欲自縊，父母曰：「汝未嫁，何得爾？

translations.literal: She again wished to hang herself; her parents said: "You are not yet married — how can you do such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: She tried to hang herself. Her parents said, "You are not yet married — how can you do this?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「女自分無活理，即如父母言，願終身稱未亡人。

translations.literal: " She replied: "A woman knows she has no reason to live; even as my parents say, I wish all my life to be called one who has not yet died.
translations.idiomatic: " She answered, "A woman in my place has no reason to live. Even as you say, I wish to spend my whole life as one who has not yet died — a widow in name if not in law.

sentences.zh: 」大聲哀號不止。

translations.literal: " She wailed aloud without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: " She wailed aloud without stopping.

sentences.zh: 及殮，剪發系夫右臂以殉。

translations.literal: At the encoffining she cut off her hair and tied it to her husband's right arm as a companion in death.
translations.idiomatic: At the encoffining she cut off her hair and bound it to her husband's right arm to accompany him in death.

sentences.zh: 抵家，告父母曰：「有婦，以事姑也。

translations.literal: On reaching home she told her parents: "I have become a wife — to serve my mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When she reached home she told her parents, "I am a wife now — my duty is to serve my mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑既失子，可並令無婦乎？

translations.literal: She has lost her son — can you also leave her without a daughter-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: She has lost her son — would you leave her without a daughter-in-law as well?

sentences.zh: 願歸羅，以畢所事」。

translations.literal: I wish to return to the Luo household, to complete what I owe in service."
translations.idiomatic: Let me return to the Luo household and finish what remains of my duty."

sentences.zh: 」父母從之。

translations.literal: Her parents consented.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents agreed.

sentences.zh: 後父知廣元縣，姑病卒，女乃歸寧。

translations.literal: Later her father served as magistrate of Guangyuan County; when her mother-in-law died of illness the girl returned to her natal home.
translations.idiomatic: Later her father was appointed magistrate of Guangyuan County. When her mother-in-law died, she returned to her parents' home.

sentences.zh: 有諷他適者，曰：「事姑畢矣，更何待？

translations.literal: Some hinted that she should marry elsewhere, saying: "Your service to your mother-in-law is finished — what more do you wait for?
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested she marry again, saying, "Your duty to your mother-in-law is done — what are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 」女曰：「我昔殮羅郎時，有一束發纏其手，誰能掘冢開棺，取發還我，則易誌矣。

translations.literal: " The girl said: "When I encoffined Master Luo, a lock of hair was wound around his hand — who could dig up the grave, open the coffin, take back my hair, and then I would change my resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "When I encoffined Master Luo, I bound a lock of hair around his hand. Unless someone digs up the grave, opens the coffin, and returns that hair to me, I will not change my mind.

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " And so they said no more.

sentences.zh: 生平獨臥一樓，年六十余卒。

translations.literal: All her life she slept alone on an upper floor; she died in her sixties.
translations.idiomatic: She lived alone on an upper floor all her life and died in her sixties.

sentences.zh: 莊氏，海康吳金童妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhuang was the wife of Wu Jintong of Haikang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhuang was the wife of Wu Jintong of Haikang.

sentences.zh: 成化初，廣西流寇掠鄉邑，莊隨夫避新會，傭劉銘家。

translations.literal: In the early Chenghua reign, Guangxi bandits plundered the district; Zhuang followed her husband to take refuge in Xinhui and was hired out to the household of Liu Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua era, bandits from Guangxi raided the region. Zhuang fled with her husband to Xinhui and went to work in the household of Liu Ming.

sentences.zh: 銘見莊美，欲犯之，屢誘不從。

translations.literal: Ming saw that Zhuang was beautiful and wished to violate her; he tempted her many times but she would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Ming found Zhuang beautiful and tried to force himself on her; he tempted her again and again, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 乃令黨梁狗同金童入海捕魚，沒水死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his follower Liang Gou together with Jintong out to sea to fish; Jintong drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his henchman Liang Gou out to sea with Jintong to fish, and Jintong drowned.

sentences.zh: 越三日不還，莊求之海賓，屍浮岸側，手足被縛，腫腐莫可辨。

translations.literal: After three days with no return, Zhuang searched along the shore; the corpse floated up beside the bank, hands and feet bound, swollen and rotted beyond recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed with no sign of him. Zhuang searched the shore and found a corpse floating there, hands and feet bound, swollen and rotted beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 莊以衣識之，歸攜女赴水，抱夫屍而沒。

translations.literal: Zhuang recognized it by the clothing, returned home, took her daughter, and went into the water, embracing her husband's corpse as she sank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang recognized him by his clothes, went home, took her daughter, and drowned herself in the water, clasping her husband's corpse as she went under.

sentences.zh: 翼日，三屍隨流繞銘門，去而復還。

translations.literal: The next day three corpses drifted with the current around Ming's gate, going away and returning again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day three corpses drifted past Ming's gate with the tide, receding and returning again.

sentences.zh: 士人感異殯祭之，然莫知銘殺也，後梁狗漏言，有司並捕考，處以極刑。

translations.literal: Scholars, moved by the marvel, gave them proper burial and sacrifice, yet none knew that Ming had killed him; later Liang Gou let slip the truth, and the authorities arrested and interrogated them all, punishing them with the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Local scholars, awed by the omen, gave the bodies proper burial and rites, though no one yet knew Ming had murdered him. Later Liang Gou let the truth slip; the authorities arrested and interrogated them all and sentenced them to death.

sentences.zh: 唐氏，汝陽陳旺妻，隨其夫以歌舞逐食四方。

translations.literal: Lady Tang was the wife of Chen Wang of Ruyang; she followed her husband in earning a living through song and dance as they wandered the land.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tang was the wife of Chen Wang of Ruyang; she traveled with him, earning their keep through song and dance.

sentences.zh: 正德三年秋，旺攜妻及女環兒、侄成兒至江夏九峰山。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Zhengde, Wang took his wife and daughter Huan'er and nephew Chenger to Jiufeng Mountain in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year of Zhengde, Wang took his wife, their daughter Huan'er, and his nephew Chenger to Jiufeng Mountain in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 有史聰者，亦以傀儡為業。

translations.literal: There was one Shi Cong who also made his living with puppet shows.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Shi Cong also made his living with puppet shows.

sentences.zh: 見婦、女皆艷麗，而旺且老，因紿旺至青山，夜殺之。

translations.literal: Seeing that the wife and daughter were both lovely while Wang was already old, he lured Wang to Qingshan and killed him by night.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that mother and daughter were both beautiful while Wang was already old, he lured Wang to Qingshan and murdered him by night.

sentences.zh: 明日，聰獨返，攜其婦、女、幼侄入武昌山吳王祠，持利刃脅唐。

translations.literal: The next day Cong returned alone, taking the wife, daughter, and young nephew into the King Wu Shrine in Wuchang Mountain, and threatened Tang with a sharp blade.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cong returned alone, brought the wife, daughter, and young nephew into the King Wu Shrine on Wuchang Mountain, and threatened Lady Tang with a drawn blade.

sentences.zh: 唐曰：「汝殺吾夫，吾不能殺汝以復仇，忍從汝亂邪？

translations.literal: Tang said: "You killed my husband. I cannot kill you to avenge him — how could I bear to submit to your debauchery?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tang said, "You murdered my husband. I cannot kill you to avenge him — how could I endure submitting to your violence?

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害。

translations.literal: " She was then murdered.
translations.idiomatic: " She was then killed.

sentences.zh: 賊裹以席，置荊棘中。

translations.literal: The bandit wrapped her in a mat and placed her among brambles.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit wrapped her in a mat and left her among the brambles.

sentences.zh: 明日，徙蓑衣園，賊又迫環兒，臨以刃。

translations.literal: The next day they moved to Suoyi Garden; the bandit again forced Huan'er, threatening her with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they moved to Suoyi Garden. The bandit again pressed Huan'er, holding a blade to her throat.

sentences.zh: 環兒哭且詈，聲振林木，賊亦殺之，瘞糞壤中而去。

translations.literal: Huan'er wept and cursed; her voice shook the trees. The bandit killed her too, buried her in filthy soil, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan'er wept and cursed until her voice shook the forest. The bandit killed her as well, buried her in dung and mud, and went his way.

sentences.zh: 其年冬至，賊被酒，成兒潛出告官，擒於葛店市，伏誅。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, the bandit was drunk. Chenger slipped out secretly to report to the authorities; he was captured at Gedian market and executed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice the bandit was drunk. Chenger slipped out to report him to the magistrate. Cong was seized at Gedian market and put to death.

sentences.zh: 王氏，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Wang, a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 聘於陳，而夫佳病，其父母娶婦以慰之。

translations.literal: Betrothed to the Chen clan, but her fiancé Jia was ill; his parents took a bride to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to the Chen family, but her fiancé Jia fell ill; his parents brought home a bride to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 及門，即入侍湯藥。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the gate she immediately entered to attend to medicines and broth.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as she entered the gate she began attending to his medicines and broth.

sentences.zh: 未幾，佳卒，王年甫十七，矢誌不嫁。

translations.literal: Before long Jia died; Wang was only seventeen and vowed never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jia died. Wang was only seventeen, and she vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 姑張氏曰：「未成禮而守，無名。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law Zhang said: "To remain faithful without having completed the rites — it has no standing.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Zhang said, "To remain chaste when the marriage rites were never completed — that has no standing.

sentences.zh: 」女曰：「入陳氏門，經事君子，何謂無名？

translations.literal: " The daughter said: "Having entered the Chen clan gate and having served a gentleman — what do you mean, it has no standing?
translations.idiomatic: " She replied, "I entered the Chen family's gate and served a husband. How can you call that nameless?

sentences.zh: 」姑乃使其二女從容諷之。

translations.literal: " The mother-in-law then had her two daughters gently admonish her with hints.
translations.idiomatic: " The mother-in-law then sent her two daughters to coax and counsel her.

sentences.zh: 婦不答，截發毀容。

translations.literal: The daughter-in-law did not answer; she cut her hair and disfigured her face.
translations.idiomatic: The young wife made no reply. She cut off her hair and disfigured her face.

sentences.zh: 姑終欲強之，窘辱萬狀。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law still sought to force her; she humiliated her in every manner.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law still tried to force remarriage on her, subjecting her to every kind of humiliation.

sentences.zh: 二小姑陵之若婢，稍不順即爪其面，姑聞復加箠楚。

translations.literal: The two sisters-in-law treated her overbearingly as if she were a maidservant; at the slightest disobedience they clawed her face, and when the mother-in-law heard of it she added beatings.
translations.idiomatic: The two sisters-in-law treated her like a servant and bullied her relentlessly; at the slightest offense they scratched her face, and when the mother-in-law heard of it she beat her as well.

sentences.zh: 女口不出怨言，曰：「不逼嫁，為婢亦甘也。

translations.literal: The girl uttered no word of complaint and said: "So long as you do not force me to remarry, even serving as a maidservant I would accept gladly.
translations.idiomatic: She never voiced a word of complaint and said, "If you do not force me to remarry, I am content even to serve as a maidservant.

sentences.zh: 」夜寢處小姑床下，受濕得傴疾，私自幸曰：「我知免矣。

translations.literal: " At night she slept beneath her sister-in-law's bed, suffered damp and contracted a hunchback; she told herself with secret relief: "Now I know I am spared.
translations.idiomatic: " At night she slept on the floor beneath her sister-in-law's bed. The damp gave her a hunched back, and she told herself with private relief, "Now I know I am spared.

sentences.zh: 」鞠從子梅為嗣，教之。

translations.literal: " She raised her nephew Mei as heir and educated him.
translations.idiomatic: " She raised her nephew Mei as heir and tutored him.

sentences.zh: 成化初領鄉薦，卒昌其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign he passed the provincial examination; in the end he glorified the family.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chenghua reign he passed the provincial examination and in time made the family prosper.

sentences.zh: 後有易氏，分宜人，嫁安福王世昌。

translations.literal: Later there was Lady Yi, a native of Fenyang, who married Wang Shichang of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Lady Yi of Fenyang, who married Wang Shichang of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 時世昌已遘疾，奄奄十余月，易事之，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: At that time Shichang had already fallen ill; for more than ten months he lingered near death, and Yi attended him without removing her girdle.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shichang was already gravely ill. For more than ten months he lingered near death, and Yi never left his side day or night.

sentences.zh: 世昌死，除喪猶縞素。

translations.literal: When Shichang died, after the mourning period she still wore plain white hemp.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichang died she continued wearing unadorned white even after the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 姑憐之，謂：「汝猶處子，可終累乎？

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law took pity on her and said: "You are still as a virgin — must you bind yourself for life?
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law took pity on her and said, "You are still a maiden in spirit — must you burden yourself for life?

sentences.zh: 」跪泣曰：「是何言哉？

translations.literal: " Kneeling, weeping, she said: "What words are these?
translations.idiomatic: " Kneeling and weeping, she said, "How can you speak such words?

sentences.zh: 父母許我王氏，即終身王氏婦矣。

translations.literal: My parents promised me to the Wang clan — thus I am a Wang woman for life.
translations.idiomatic: When my parents betrothed me to the Wang family, I became a Wang wife for life.

sentences.zh: 」自是獨處一樓，不窺外戶四十余年。

translations.literal: " From then on she lived alone on one upper floor and for more than forty years never looked out the outer door.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on she lived alone on one upper floor and for more than forty years never so much as glanced outside.

sentences.zh: 方世昌疾，所吐痰血，輒手一布囊盛之。

translations.literal: While Shichang was ill, whenever he spat phlegm and blood she would take a cloth sack and collect it by hand.
translations.idiomatic: During Shichang's illness she would save every drop of phlegm and blood he coughed up in a cloth pouch.

sentences.zh: 卒後，用所盛囊為枕，枕之終身。

translations.literal: After he died she used the sack that held them as a pillow and slept on it all her life.
translations.idiomatic: After he died she made that pouch her pillow and slept on it for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 鐘氏，桐城陶鏞妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhong, wife of Tao Yong of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhong was the wife of Tao Yong of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 鏞以罪被戍，卒於外。

translations.literal: Yong was sentenced to frontier service for a crime and died abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was banished for a crime and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 鐘年二十五，子繼甫在抱，負鏞骨四千餘里歸葬。

translations.literal: Zhong was twenty-five; her son Jifu was still in arms. She carried Yong's bones more than four thousand li home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was twenty-five. Her son Jifu was still an infant in her arms. She carried her husband's bones more than four thousand li home for burial.

sentences.zh: 乃斷發杜門，年八十二以節終。

translations.literal: She then cut her hair and shut her door; at eighty-two she ended her chaste widowhood in death.
translations.idiomatic: She then cut her hair and shut herself indoors. At eighty-two she died, having kept her vow to the end.

sentences.zh: 繼亦早卒，妻方氏年二十七，子亮甫二歲。

translations.literal: Ji also died early; his wife Lady Fang was twenty-seven, and their son Liangfu was two.
translations.idiomatic: Ji also died young. His wife Lady Fang was twenty-seven, and their son Liangfu was two.

sentences.zh: 其兄憐之，微叩其意，方以死誓。

translations.literal: Her elder brother took pity on her and subtly probed her intentions; Fang swore by death.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother took pity on her and tactfully sounded her out about remarriage; Fang vowed she would die before remarrying.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，亮舉鄉試，業於太學，卒。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign Liang passed the provincial examination and studied at the Imperial Academy, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign Liang passed the provincial examination and studied at the Imperial Academy, but then died.

sentences.zh: 妻王氏年二十八，妾吳氏二十二，皆無子，扶櫬歸葬。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wang was twenty-eight, his concubine Lady Wu twenty-two; both were childless. They escorted the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wang was twenty-eight and his concubine Lady Wu was twenty-two. Neither had borne a child. Together they escorted his coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 貧不能支，所親勸之嫁，兩人哭曰：「而不知我之為節婦婦乎！

translations.literal: Poor and unable to sustain themselves, their kin urged them to remarry. The two wept and said: "Do you not know what it means to be wives in a line of chaste widowhood?
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to support themselves, their relatives urged them to remarry. Both women wept and said, "Do you not know that we are wives in a house of chaste widows?

sentences.zh: 」乃共以紡績自給。

translations.literal: " They then together supported themselves by spinning and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: " They then supported themselves together by spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 越二十六年，縣令陳勉以聞，詔旌三代。

translations.literal: After twenty-six years, Magistrate Chen Mian reported it; an edict honored three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six years later Magistrate Chen Mian reported the case to the throne, and an imperial edict honored all three generations.

sentences.zh: 人稱之曰四節裏。

translations.literal: People called it the Lane of Four Chaste Widows.
translations.idiomatic: People called their lane the Lane of Four Chaste Widows.

sentences.zh: 宣氏，嘉定張樹田妻。

translations.literal: Lady Xuan, wife of Zhang Shutian of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xuan was the wife of Zhang Shutian of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 夫素狂悖，與宣不睦。

translations.literal: Her husband had always been wild and perverse; he and Xuan were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband had always been violent and unreasonable, and he and Xuan did not get along.

sentences.zh: 夫病，宣晨夕奉事。

translations.literal: When her husband fell ill, Xuan attended him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband fell ill, Xuan attended him day and night.

sentences.zh: 及死，誓身殉。

translations.literal: When he died she vowed to follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: When he died she vowed to die with him.

sentences.zh: 時樹田友人沈思道亦死，其婦孫與宣以死相要，各分尺帛。

translations.literal: At that time Shutian's friend Shen Sidao had also died; his wife Sun and Xuan pledged death to each other, each taking a foot of silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shutian's friend Shen Sidao had also died. His wife Sun and Xuan pledged to die together and each cut a length of silk cloth for the purpose.

sentences.zh: 孫自經，或勸宣曰：「彼與夫相得，故以死報，汝何為效之？

translations.literal: Sun hanged herself. Some urged Xuan, saying: "She and her husband were close, hence she repaid him with death — why should you imitate her?
translations.idiomatic: Sun hanged herself. Some tried to dissuade Xuan, saying, "She and her husband were devoted to each other, so she died with him — why should you do the same?

sentences.zh: 」宣嘆曰：「予知盡婦道而已，安論夫之賢不賢。

translations.literal: " Xuan sighed and said: "I know only to fulfill a wife's duty — why discuss whether the husband is worthy or unworthy?
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan sighed and said, "I know only to fulfill my duty as a wife. What does it matter whether the husband was worthy or not?

sentences.zh: 」卒縊死。

translations.literal: " In the end she hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 徐氏，慈谿人，定海金傑妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Xu, a native of Cixi, wife of Jin Jie of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu was a native of Cixi and the wife of Jin Jie of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 成化中，傑兄以罪逮入京，傑往請代。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign Jie's elder brother was arrested for a crime and taken to the capital; Jie went to ask to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign Jie's elder brother was arrested for a crime and taken to the capital. Jie went to offer himself in his brother's place.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，徐已有身，傑謂曰：「予去，生死不可知，若生男善撫之，金氏鬼庶得食也。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Xu was already with child. Jie said to her: "When I go, life or death cannot be known. If you bear a son, raise him well — then the Jin clan's dead may at least receive offerings.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Xu was already pregnant. Jie told her, "When I go I may not return. If you bear a son, raise him well so that the Jin ancestors may at least receive offerings.

sentences.zh: 」已而悔曰：「我幾誤汝，吾去無還理，即死，善事後人。

translations.literal: " Then he regretted and said: "I nearly misled you. When I go there is no reason to return; when I die, serve well those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he reconsidered and said, "I almost misled you. I will not return. When I am dead, serve those who come after me well.

sentences.zh: 」徐泣曰：「君以義往，上必義君，君兄弟當同歸，無過苦也。

translations.literal: " Xu wept and said: "My lord goes for righteousness; the sovereign will surely respond with righteousness. Your brothers should return together — do not grieve overmuch.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu wept and said, "You go for righteousness; the emperor will surely respond in kind. Your brothers will return together — do not grieve too much.

sentences.zh: 即如君言，妾有死耳，敢忘付托乎？

translations.literal: Even if it happens as you say, I have only death — how could I forget your charge?
translations.idiomatic: Even if it happens as you say, I would die rather than fail you — how could I forget what you have entrusted to me?

sentences.zh: 」已果生男，無何兄得還，傑竟瘐死。

translations.literal: " In time she indeed bore a son. Before long the elder brother was released and returned; Jie ultimately died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: " In time she bore a son. Before long the elder brother was released and returned, but Jie died in prison after all.

sentences.zh: 徐撫孤慟曰：「我本欲從汝父地下，奈金氏何？

translations.literal: Xu embraced the orphan in grief and said: "I originally wished to follow your father to the underworld — but what would become of the Jin clan?
translations.idiomatic: Xu held the orphaned boy and wept, "I meant to follow your father to the grave — but what would become of the Jin clan?

sentences.zh: 」強營葬事。

translations.literal: " She forced herself to arrange the burial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " She forced herself to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 服闋，父母勸他適，截發斷指自誓，食淡茹苦六十余年，視子孫再世成立，乃卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended her parents urged another marriage; she cut her hair and severed a finger to swear herself, eating plain food and enduring hardship for more than sixty years; she saw grandsons and great-grandsons established through two generations, then died.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended her parents urged her to remarry. She cut her hair and severed a finger to bind her oath, and for more than sixty years lived in austerity and hardship. She lived to see her sons and grandsons prosper through two generations, and then died.

sentences.zh: 義妾張氏，南京人。

translations.literal: The faithful concubine Lady Zhang, a native of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang the faithful concubine was a native of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 松江楊玉山商南京，娶為妾。

translations.literal: Yang Yushan of Songjiang traded in Nanjing and took her as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yushan of Songjiang was trading in Nanjing when he took her as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 逾月以婦妒，遣之歸。

translations.literal: After more than a month, because the principal wife was jealous, he sent her back.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month his principal wife's jealousy drove him to send Zhang home.

sentences.zh: 張屏居自守，楊亦數往來，所贈千計。

translations.literal: Zhang lived alone in seclusion and kept herself chaste; Yang also came and went several times; his gifts numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang lived alone and kept herself chaste. Yang still visited from time to time, and his gifts over the years numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 後二十余年，楊坐役累，罄其產，怏怏失明。

translations.literal: More than twenty years later Yang was implicated in corvée labor, lost all his property, and in dejection went blind.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years later Yang was ruined by corvée obligations, lost everything he owned, and in despair went blind.

sentences.zh: 張聞之，直造楊廬，拜主母，捧楊袂大慟。

translations.literal: When Zhang heard, she went straight to Yang's dwelling, bowed to the principal wife, grasped Yang's sleeve, and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang heard the news she went straight to Yang's home, bowed to the principal wife, seized Yang's sleeve, and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 乃悉出向所贈金珠，具裝，嫁其二女，並為二子娶婦，留侍湯藥。

translations.literal: She then brought out in full all the gold and jewels he had formerly given her, provided dowries, married off his two daughters, and found wives for both sons as well, remaining to attend to medicines and broth.
translations.idiomatic: She then brought out all the gold and jewels he had given her over the years, provided dowries for his two daughters, found wives for both sons, and stayed on to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 逾年楊死，守其柩不去。

translations.literal: After more than a year Yang died; she kept watch over his coffin and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later Yang died. She kept vigil over his coffin and would not leave it.

sentences.zh: 既免喪，父母強之歸，不從，矢誌以歿，終身不見一人。

translations.literal: After mourning was completed her parents forced her to return home; she would not obey, vowed herself until death, and all her life did not receive a single visitor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended her parents tried to force her home, but she refused. She vowed to keep faith until death and for the rest of her life received no visitor.

sentences.zh: 龔烈婦，江陰人。

translations.literal: Gong the Chaste Wife, a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Gong the Chaste Wife was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 年十七嫁劉玉，家貧，力作養姑。

translations.literal: At seventeen she married Liu Yu; the family was poor, and by hard labor she supported her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen she married Liu Yu. The family was poor, and she supported her mother-in-law through hard labor.

sentences.zh: 姑亡，相夫營葬。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died she assisted her husband in arranging burial.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died she helped her husband arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 夫又亡，無以為斂。

translations.literal: Her husband also died; there was no means to encoffin him.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband died in turn, and they had no means to bury him properly.

sentences.zh: 裏有羨婦色者，欲助以棺。

translations.literal: In the neighborhood was one who admired the wife's beauty and wished to provide a coffin as help.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor who coveted her beauty offered to provide a coffin.

sentences.zh: 龔覺其意，辭之。

translations.literal: Gong perceived his intent and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Gong understood his intent and refused.

sentences.zh: 既又強之，龔恐無以自脫，乃以所生六歲男、三歲女寄食母家。

translations.literal: When he again pressed her, Gong feared she could not escape; she sent her six-year-old son and three-year-old daughter born to her to live on her mother's household for food.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed her again, Gong feared she could not escape him. She sent her six-year-old son and three-year-old daughter to live with her mother.

sentences.zh: 是夜，積麥稿屋中，舉火自焚，抱夫屍死。

translations.literal: That night she heaped wheat straw inside the house, set fire and burned herself, embracing her husband's corpse to die.
translations.idiomatic: That night she piled wheat straw in the house, set it ablaze, and burned herself to death while embracing her husband's corpse.

sentences.zh: 又江氏，蒙城王可道妻。

translations.literal: Also Lady Jiang, wife of Wang Kedao of Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Jiang, wife of Wang Kedao of Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 夫貧，負販糊口，死不能斂。

translations.literal: Her husband was poor; he peddled goods on his back to feed his mouth, and when he died could not be encoffined.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband was poor. He peddled goods for a living, and when he died the family could not afford a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 比鄰諸生李雲蟾合錢斂之，卜日以葬。

translations.literal: The neighboring licentiate Li Yunchan pooled money to encoffin him and chose a day for burial.
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring licentiate named Li Yunchan collected funds for a coffin and set a day for the burial.

sentences.zh: 及期，率眾至其家，闃然無聲，廚下燈微明，趨視之飲食畢具，蓋以待舁棺者，婦已縊死竈旁矣。

translations.literal: When the day arrived he led the crowd to their home; all was silent. A lamp in the kitchen burned dimly; they hurried to look — food and drink were all prepared, evidently to await those who would carry the coffin; the wife had already hanged herself beside the stove.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived he led the mourners to their home. All was silent. A lamp burned dimly in the kitchen. They rushed to look and found food and drink laid out, evidently prepared for those who would carry the coffin. The wife had already hanged herself beside the stove.

sentences.zh: 眾驚嘆，復合錢並葬之。

translations.literal: The crowd marveled and sighed; they pooled money again and buried them together.
translations.idiomatic: The mourners were stunned. They collected money again and buried husband and wife together.

sentences.zh: 會稽範氏二女，幼好讀書，並通《列女傳》。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Fan clan of Kuaiji loved reading from childhood and both mastered the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters of the Fan clan of Kuaiji loved to read from childhood and both mastered the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 長適江，一月寡。

translations.literal: The elder married into the Jiang clan and was widowed after one month.
translations.idiomatic: The elder married into the Jiang family and was widowed after only a month.

sentences.zh: 次將歸傅，而夫亡。

translations.literal: The younger was about to be married to the Fu clan when her fiancé died.
translations.idiomatic: The younger was betrothed to the Fu family when her fiancé died before the wedding.

sentences.zh: 二女同守節，築高垣，圍田十畝，穿井其中，為屋三楹以居。

translations.literal: The two daughters together preserved chastity, built a high wall, enclosed ten mu of fields, dug a well within, and made a dwelling of three bays to live in.
translations.idiomatic: The two sisters vowed to remain chaste together. They built a high wall around ten mu of fields, dug a well inside, and made a three-room house to live in.

sentences.zh: 當種獲，父啟圭竇率傭以入，余日則塞其竇，共汲井灌田。

translations.literal: At planting and harvest their father opened a small hole in the wall and led hired laborers in; on other days they blocked the hole, and together drew water from the well to irrigate the fields.
translations.idiomatic: At planting and harvest their father would open a small hole in the wall and let hired laborers in. On all other days they sealed it shut and drew water from their well together to irrigate the fields.

sentences.zh: 如是者三十年。

translations.literal: Thus for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: They lived this way for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 自為塋於屋後，成化中卒，竟合葬焉。

translations.literal: They made their own graves behind the house; in the Chenghua reign they died and were at last buried together there.
translations.idiomatic: They prepared their own graves behind the house. They died during the Chenghua reign and were buried together there.

sentences.zh: 族人即其田立祠以祀。

translations.literal: The clansmen established a shrine on their land to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The clan built a shrine on their land to honor them.

sentences.zh: 又有丁美音，漵浦丁正明女。

translations.literal: Also Ding Meiyin, daughter of Ding Zhengming of Xupu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ding Meiyin, daughter of Ding Zhengming of Xupu.

sentences.zh: 幼受夏學程聘，年十八將嫁，學程死，美音誓不再嫁。

translations.literal: From childhood she received betrothal from Xia Xuecheng; at eighteen she was about to marry when Xuecheng died; Meiyin vowed never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was betrothed to Xia Xuecheng. At eighteen, just before the wedding, Xuecheng died. Meiyin vowed never to marry another.

sentences.zh: 父母曰：「未嫁守節，非禮也。

translations.literal: Her parents said: "To preserve chastity without having married is not according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents said, "To remain chaste without ever having married is not proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 何自苦如此？

translations.literal: Why afflict yourself so?
translations.idiomatic: Why torment yourself like this?

sentences.zh: 」美音嚙指滴血，籲天自矢。

translations.literal: " Meiyin bit her finger until blood flowed and called to Heaven to bind her oath.
translations.idiomatic: " Meiyin bit her finger until blood dripped, then called upon Heaven to witness her vow.

sentences.zh: 當道交旌之，賫以銀幣約百金，乃構室獨居，鬻田自贍，事舅姑，養父母。

translations.literal: The local authorities together honored her; they bestowed silver worth about a hundred gold, whereupon she built a room and lived alone, sold fields to support herself, served her parents-in-law, and nourished her own parents.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities jointly honored her and presented silver worth about a hundred taels. She built a room and lived alone, sold fields to support herself, cared for her parents-in-law, and provided for her own parents.

sentences.zh: 鄉人名其田為貞女田。

translations.literal: Villagers named her field the Field of the Chaste Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers named her field the Field of the Chaste Maiden.

sentences.zh: 成氏，無錫人，定陶教諭繒女，登封訓導尤輔妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Cheng, a native of Wuxi, daughter of Instructor Zeng of Dingtao, wife of Assistant Instructor You Fu of Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng was a native of Wuxi, daughter of Instructor Zeng of Dingtao and wife of Assistant Instructor You Fu of Dengfeng.

sentences.zh: 輔遊學靖江，成從焉。

translations.literal: Fu traveled to study at Jingjiang; Cheng followed him there.
translations.idiomatic: Fu went to Jingjiang to study, and Cheng accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 江水夜溢，家人倉卒升屋，成整衣欲上，問：「爾等衣邪？

translations.literal: The river waters overflowed by night; the household in haste climbed onto the roof. Cheng straightened her clothes intending to ascend and asked: "Are you all clothed?
translations.idiomatic: The river burst its banks in the night. The household scrambled onto the roof in panic. Cheng straightened her garments before climbing up and asked, "Are you all dressed?

sentences.zh: 」眾謝不暇。

translations.literal: " The crowd apologized that there was no time.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone cried that there had been no time.

sentences.zh: 成曰：「安有男女裸，而尚可俱生邪？

translations.literal: Cheng said: "How can there be naked men and women, and yet they can still live together?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "How can men and women be stripped bare and still go on living together?

sentences.zh: 我獨留死耳。

translations.literal: I alone will remain to die."
translations.idiomatic: I alone will stay behind to die."

sentences.zh: 」眾號哭請，不應。

translations.literal: " The crowd wailed and pleaded; she did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd wept and begged her; she gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 厥明，水退，坐死榻上。

translations.literal: At dawn the waters receded; she sat dead upon the couch.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the flood withdrew. She was found seated dead upon the couch.

sentences.zh: 後崇禎中，興安大水，漂沒廬舍。

translations.literal: Later in the Chongzhen reign, Xing'an suffered a great flood that washed away houses.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Chongzhen reign, a great flood struck Xing'an and swept away homes.

sentences.zh: 有結筏自救者，鄰裏多附之。

translations.literal: Some built rafts to save themselves, and many neighbors attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: Some lashed together rafts to save themselves, and many neighbors clung to them.

sentences.zh: 二女子附一朽木，倏沈倏浮，引筏救之，年皆十六七，問其姓氏不答。

translations.literal: Two girls clung to a rotten log, now sinking now floating; a raft was sent to rescue them. Both were sixteen or seventeen; asked their surnames, they did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Two girls clung to a rotting log, sinking and surfacing by turns, until a raft pulled them aboard. Both were sixteen or seventeen. When asked their names, they would not answer.

sentences.zh: 二女見筏上男子有裸者，嘆曰：「吾姊妹倚木不死，冀有善地可存也，今若此，何用生為！

translations.literal: The two girls saw men on the raft who were naked, and sighed: "We sisters clung to this log and did not die, hoping to find some decent place where we could survive—yet now it comes to this. What use is living?
translations.idiomatic: When the two girls saw naked men on the raft, they sighed, "We sisters held to this log and lived only in hope of reaching some proper place. Now that we face this—what is the point of going on?

sentences.zh: 」攜手躍入波中死。

translations.literal: " Hand in hand they leaped into the waves and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Taking each other's hands, they leaped into the waves and drowned.

sentences.zh: 章銀兒，蘭谿人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yiner, a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yiner was a native of Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，獨與母居。

translations.literal: He lost his father in youth and lived alone with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father as a boy and lived alone with his mother.

sentences.zh: 邑多火災，室盡毀，結茅以棲母。

translations.literal: The district suffered many fires; their house was completely destroyed, and he built a thatched hut to shelter his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Fires ravaged the district until their home was destroyed. He built a thatched hut to shelter his mother.

sentences.zh: 母方疾，鄰居又火，銀兒出視，眾呼令疾避。

translations.literal: His mother was ill; another fire broke out among the neighbors. Yiner went out to look; the crowd shouted for him to flee quickly.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was ill when fire broke out next door. Yiner stepped outside to look, and the crowd shouted for him to run.

sentences.zh: 銀兒曰：「母疾不能動，何可獨避。

translations.literal: Yiner said: "Mother is ill and cannot move. How could I flee alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yiner said, "Mother is too ill to move. How could I flee alone?

sentences.zh: 」亟返入廬，欲扶母出，烈焰忽覆其廬，眾莫能救。

translations.literal: " He hurried back into the hut intending to help his mother out, but suddenly flames engulfed the hut and none could save them.
translations.idiomatic: " He rushed back inside to help his mother out, but flames suddenly engulfed the hut, and no one could save them.

sentences.zh: 火光中，遙見銀兒抱其母，宛轉同焚死，時弘治元年三月也。

translations.literal: In the firelight they saw from afar Yiner embracing his mother; writhing together they were burned to death. It was the third month of the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Through the flames they saw Yiner from afar, holding his mother in his arms as the two writhed and burned together. It was the third month of the first year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 義妹茅氏，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Righteous Maiden Mao, a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous maiden Mao was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 年十四，父母亡，獨與兄嫂居。

translations.literal: At fourteen, her parents died; she lived alone with her elder brother and sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she lost both parents and lived with her elder brother and sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 其兄病痿臥。

translations.literal: Her elder brother was afflicted with paralysis and lay bedridden.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother was paralyzed and bedridden.

sentences.zh: 值倭入縣，嫂出奔，呼與偕行。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates entered the county, the sister-in-law fled and called her to go together.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese raiders entered the county, her sister-in-law fled and called for her to come along.

sentences.zh: 女曰：「我室女，將安之！

translations.literal: The girl said: "I am an unmarried maiden—where would I go!
translations.idiomatic: The girl said, "I am an unmarried girl—where would I go!

sentences.zh: 且俱去，誰扶吾兄者！

translations.literal: And if we all leave, who will support my brother!
translations.idiomatic: And if we all flee, who will support my brother!

sentences.zh: 」賊至，縱火，女力扶其兄避於空室，竟被燔灼並死。

translations.literal: " The bandits arrived and set fires. The girl strenuously supported her brother and hid with him in an empty room, but in the end they were burned together and died.
translations.idiomatic: " The raiders came and set fires. The girl strained to support her brother and hide with him in an empty room, but in the end they were burned together and died.

sentences.zh: 招囊猛，雲南孟璉長官司土官舍人刁派羅妻也。

translations.literal: Zhao Nangmeng was wife of Diao Pailuo, a steward of the native chieftain of Menglian Chief's Office in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nangmeng was the wife of Diao Pailuo, a steward in the native chieftain's household of Menglian Chief's Office in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，夫死，守節二十八年。

translations.literal: At twenty-five her husband died; she preserved chastity for twenty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-five when her husband died, and she preserved her chastity for twenty-eight years.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年九月，雲南都指揮使奏其事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Hongzhi, the Regional Military Commissioner of Yunnan reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Hongzhi, the regional military commissioner of Yunnan reported her case.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以天下為家，方思勵名教以變夷俗。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I take all under Heaven as my home and am just now seeking to encourage the norms of teaching to transform barbarian customs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I take all under Heaven as my home and am now seeking to uphold the norms of moral teaching and transform barbarian customs.

sentences.zh: 其有趨於禮義者，烏可不亟加獎勵。

translations.literal: Those who turn toward ritual and righteousness—how can we not promptly reward them?
translations.idiomatic: Those who turn toward ritual and righteousness—how can we fail to reward them at once?

sentences.zh: 招囊猛貞節可嘉，其即令有司顯其門閭，使遠夷益知向化，無俟核報。」

translations.literal: Zhao Nangmeng's chastity is commendable. Order the local authorities at once to honor her gate and household, so that distant barbarians will better know to turn toward civilization—without waiting for verification and report."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nangmeng's chastity is worthy of praise. Order the local authorities at once to honor her gate and household, so that distant peoples may better know to turn toward civilization—without waiting for further verification."

sentences.zh: 張維妻淩氏，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Ling, wife of Zhang Wei, a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ling, wife of Zhang Wei, was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，維舉於鄉，卒。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Wei passed the provincial examination and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Wei passed the provincial examinations and then died.

sentences.zh: 婦年二十五，子四歲亦卒。

translations.literal: The wife was twenty-five; their four-year-old son also died.
translations.idiomatic: The wife was twenty-five; their four-year-old son died as well.

sentences.zh: 其兄諷之改圖，婦痛哭嚙唇，噀血灑地，終身不歸寧。

translations.literal: Her elder brother hinted that she should change her plans; the wife wept bitterly, bit her lips, spat blood upon the ground, and never returned to her natal home for visits.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother hinted that she should change course. The wife wept until she bit her lips and spat blood on the ground, and she never again returned to her natal home.

sentences.zh: 舅姑慰之曰：「不幸絕嗣，日計無賴，吾二人景逼矣，爾年尚遠，何以為活？

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law comforted her: "Our line is unhappily cut off; day by day we have no one to depend on. The two of us are pressed by declining years, and you are still young—how will you live?
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law tried to comfort her: "Our line is cut off, and day by day we have no one to rely on. We two are pressed by old age, and you are still young—how will you live?

sentences.zh: 」婦曰：「恥辱事重，餓死甘之。

translations.literal: " The wife said: "Disgrace weighs heavily; to starve to death I would accept willingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The wife said, "Disgrace weighs more heavily than death. I would gladly starve.

sentences.zh: 」乃出簪珥為舅納妾，果得子，喜曰：「張氏不絕，亡夫墓門且有寒食矣。

translations.literal: " She then sold her hairpins and earrings to obtain a concubine for her father-in-law. A son was indeed born. She rejoiced: "The Zhang line is not cut off; my dead husband's tomb will yet know the Cold Food Festival.
translations.idiomatic: " She sold her hairpins and earrings to obtain a concubine for her father-in-law. A son was born. She rejoiced, "The Zhang line is not cut off. My dead husband's tomb will yet know the Cold Food Festival.

sentences.zh: 」後舅病瘋，姑雙目瞽，婦紡績供養，二十年不衰。

translations.literal: " Later the father-in-law fell ill with paralysis; the mother-in-law went blind in both eyes. The wife spun and wove to support them—for twenty years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: " Later her father-in-law was stricken with paralysis and her mother-in-law went blind in both eyes. The wife spun and wove to support them, and did not flag for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 後有杜氏，貴池曹桂妻。

translations.literal: There was also Lady Du, wife of Cao Gui of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Du, wife of Cao Gui of Guichi.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，夫亡，遺腹生女，悲苦無計。

translations.literal: At twenty-four her husband died; she bore a daughter posthumously and was overwhelmed with grief, with no plan for what to do.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-four when her husband died. She bore a daughter after his death and was overwhelmed with grief, with no way forward.

sentences.zh: 日諷姑為舅納妾，果生一子。

translations.literal: Day after day she urged her mother-in-law to obtain a concubine for her father-in-law; a son was indeed born.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day she urged her mother-in-law to obtain a concubine for her father-in-law, and a son was indeed born.

sentences.zh: 產後，妾死，杜以己女托於族母，而自乳其叔。

translations.literal: After the birth the concubine died. Du entrusted her own daughter to a clanswoman and herself nursed her husband's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: After the birth the concubine died. Du entrusted her own daughter to a clanswoman and nursed her husband's younger brother herself.

sentences.zh: 逾年翁喪，勸者曰：「汝辛苦撫孤，寧能以叔後汝乎？

translations.literal: After a year the father-in-law died. Those who urged her said: "You have labored hard to raise this orphan—can you truly let your uncle inherit for you?
translations.idiomatic: A year later her father-in-law died. Those who counseled her said, "You have toiled to raise this orphan—can you truly let your uncle succeed in your place?

sentences.zh: 」杜曰：「叔後吾翁，異日生二子，即以一子後我夫，吾誌畢矣。

translations.literal: " Du said: "Let my uncle succeed my father-in-law. When in time he bears two sons, one will be made heir to my husband—then my purpose will be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " Du said, "Let my uncle succeed my father-in-law. When he bears two sons in time, one will be made heir to my husband—then my purpose will be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」後卒如其言。

translations.literal: " Later it came to pass exactly as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end it came to pass exactly as she had said.

sentences.zh: 義婦楊氏，王世昌妻，臨漳人。

translations.literal: Righteous wife Yang, wife of Wang Shichang, a native of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous wife Yang, wife of Wang Shichang, was a native of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，世昌兄坐事論死。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, Shichang's elder brother was condemned to death for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Shichang's elder brother was condemned to death for a crime.

sentences.zh: 世昌念兄為嫡子，請代其刑。

translations.literal: Shichang, considering that his brother was the eldest son, asked to take his punishment in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang, knowing his brother was the eldest son, asked to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 時楊未笄，謀於父母宗族曰：「彼代兄死為義士，我顧不能為義婦邪？

translations.literal: Yang, not yet having come of age, consulted her parents and clan: "He would die in his brother's place as a man of righteousness—could I not be a righteous wife?
translations.idiomatic: Yang, not yet of age, consulted her parents and clan: "He would die in his brother's place as a man of righteousness—could I not be a righteous wife?

sentences.zh: 願訴於上代夫死。

translations.literal: I wish to petition the throne to die in my husband's place.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to petition the throne to die in my husband's place.

sentences.zh: 」遂入京陳情，敕法司議，夫妻並得釋。

translations.literal: " She went to the capital and stated her plea. An edict ordered the judicial authorities to consider the matter, and husband and wife were both released.
translations.idiomatic: " She went to the capital and stated her plea. An edict ordered the judicial authorities to consider the matter, and husband and wife were both released.

sentences.zh: 史氏，杞縣人。

translations.literal: Lady Shi, a native of Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi was a native of Qixian.

sentences.zh: 字孔弘業，未嫁而夫卒。

translations.literal: Betrothed to Kong Hongye; before marriage her betrothed died.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Kong Hongye, but before the wedding her fiancé died.

sentences.zh: 欲往殉之，母不許。

translations.literal: She wished to go and die with him; her mother would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to go and die with him, but her mother would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 女七日不食，母持茗逼之飲，雙蛾適墮杯中死，女指示曰：「物意尚孚我心，母獨不諒人邪！

translations.literal: The girl fasted seven days without eating. Her mother held out tea and pressed her to drink; two moths happened to fall into the cup and died. The girl pointed and said: "Even these creatures understand my heart—does Mother alone not understand me!
translations.idiomatic: The girl fasted for seven days. Her mother held out tea and pressed her to drink; two moths chanced to fall into the cup and died. The girl pointed and said, "Even these creatures understand my heart—does Mother alone not understand me!

sentences.zh: 」母知不可奪，翌日制素衣縞裳，送之孔氏。

translations.literal: " Her mother knew her resolve could not be changed. The next day she made plain white upper garment and hemp mourning skirt and sent her to the Kong household.
translations.idiomatic: " Her mother knew her resolve could not be changed. The next day she made a plain white upper garment and hemp mourning skirt and sent her to the Kong household.

sentences.zh: 及暮，辭舅姑，整衣自經死。

translations.literal: At evening she took leave of her parents-in-law, straightened her garments, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk she took leave of her parents-in-law, straightened her garments, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 白氣縷縷勝屋上，達旦始消。

translations.literal: Wisps of white vapor rose above the roof and did not dissipate until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Wisps of white vapor rose above the roof and did not fade until dawn.

sentences.zh: 又有林端娘者，甌寧人，字陳廷策。

translations.literal: There was also Lin Duanniang, a native of Ouning, betrothed to Chen Tingce.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lin Duanniang of Ouning, betrothed to Chen Tingce.

sentences.zh: 聞廷策訃，寄聲曰：「勿殮，吾將就死。

translations.literal: Upon hearing of Tingce's death, she sent word: "Do not encoffin him—I am coming to die.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard of Tingce's death, she sent word: "Do not encoffin him—I am coming to die.

sentences.zh: 」父曰：「而雖許字，未納幣也。

translations.literal: " Her father said: "Though you were promised in marriage, the betrothal gifts have not yet been exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: " Her father said, "Though you were promised in marriage, the betrothal gifts have not yet been exchanged.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「既詐矣，何幣之問？

translations.literal: " She replied: "Since the promise was made, what need to ask about gifts?
translations.idiomatic: " She replied, "Since the promise was made, what need to ask about gifts?

sentences.zh: 」父謹防之。

translations.literal: " Her father guarded her closely.
translations.idiomatic: " Her father guarded her closely.

sentences.zh: 曰：「女奚所不可死，顧死夫家韙耳。

translations.literal: She said: "Where may a woman not die? Only to die at her husband's house is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Where may a woman not die? Only to die at her husband's house is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」父曰：「婿家貧，無以周身。

translations.literal: " Her father said: "The groom's family is poor—there is no means to clothe you properly.
translations.idiomatic: " Her father said, "The groom's family is poor—there is no means to clothe you properly.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「身非所恤。

translations.literal: " She said: "My person is not what I care about.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "My person is not what I care about.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「婿家貧，孰為標名？

translations.literal: " He again said: "The groom's family is poor—who would raise a monument to your name?
translations.idiomatic: " He again said, "The groom's family is poor—who would raise a monument to your name?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「名非所求。

translations.literal: " She said: "Renown is not what I seek.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "Renown is not what I seek.

sentences.zh: 」遂往哭奠畢，自克死期，理帛自經，三拱而絕。

translations.literal: " She went, wept and made offerings, fixed her own day of death, arranged silk cord and hanged herself—three convulsions and she was dead.
translations.idiomatic: " She went, wept and made offerings, fixed her own day of death, arranged a silk cord and hanged herself—three convulsions and she was dead.

sentences.zh: 陳故家青陽山下，山下人言婦將盡時，山鳴三晝夜。

translations.literal: The Chen family home was below Mount Qingyang. People below the mountain say that as the wife neared her end, the mountain roared for three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen family home stood below Mount Qingyang. People below the mountain say that as the wife neared her end, the mountain roared for three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 汪烈婦，晉江諸生楊希閔妻也。

translations.literal: The chaste wife Wang, wife of Yang Ximin, a licentiate of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste wife Wang was the wife of Yang Ximin, a licentiate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，夫死，無子，欲自經。

translations.literal: At twenty-three her husband died; having no son, she wished to hang herself.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-three when her husband died. Having no son, she wished to hang herself.

sentences.zh: 家人防之謹，不得間。

translations.literal: Her family guarded her closely and she found no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Her family guarded her closely, and she found no opportunity.

sentences.zh: 氏聞茉莉有毒能殺人，多方求之，家人不知也，日供數百朵。

translations.literal: The lady heard that jasmine was poisonous and could kill; she sought it by every means. Her family did not know, and each day supplied her hundreds of blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: The lady heard that jasmine was poisonous and could kill. She sought it by every means, while her family, unaware, supplied her hundreds of blossoms each day.

sentences.zh: 逾月，家人為亡者齋祭，婦自撰祭文，辭甚悲。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the family performed a memorial service for the deceased. The wife herself composed the sacrificial text—its words were deeply mournful.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, the family held a memorial service for the dead. The wife herself composed the sacrificial text—its words were deeply mournful.

sentences.zh: 夜五鼓，防者稍懈，取所積花煎飲之，天明死。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch of the night the guards slackened slightly; she took the flowers she had accumulated, brewed and drank them, and was dead by dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch of the night the guards slackened. She brewed the flowers she had saved and drank them, and was dead by dawn.

sentences.zh: 竇妙善，京師崇文坊人。

translations.literal: Dou Miaoshan, a native of Chongwen Ward in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Miaoshan was a native of Chongwen Ward in the capital.

sentences.zh: 年十五，為工部主事余姚姜榮妾。

translations.literal: At fifteen she became concubine of Jiang Rong of Yuyao, a principal officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen she became the concubine of Jiang Rong of Yuyao, a principal officer in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 正德中，榮以瑞州通判攝府事。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, Rong as Tongpan of Ruizhou served as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign, Rong served as acting prefect while holding the post of vice-prefect of Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 華林賊起，寇瑞，榮出走。

translations.literal: The Hualin rebels rose; they raided Ruizhou and Rong fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin rebels rose in revolt, raided Ruizhou, and Rong fled.

sentences.zh: 賊入城，執其妻及婢數人，問榮所在。

translations.literal: The rebels entered the city, seized his wife and several maidservants, and asked where Rong was.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered the city, seized his wife and several maidservants, and demanded to know where Rong was.

sentences.zh: 時妙善居別室，急取府印，開後窗投荷池。

translations.literal: Miaoshan was in a separate room; she hurriedly took the prefectural seal, opened the rear window, and cast it into the lotus pond.
translations.idiomatic: Miaoshan was in a separate room. She hurriedly took the prefectural seal, opened the rear window, and cast it into the lotus pond.

sentences.zh: 衣鮮衣前曰：「太守統援兵數千，出東門捕爾等，旦夕授首，安得執吾婢？

translations.literal: She put on fine clothes and came forward: "The prefect has led several thousand relief troops and gone out the east gate to capture you. Any day now you will lose your heads—how dare you seize my maidservants?
translations.idiomatic: She dressed in fine clothes and came forward: "The prefect has led several thousand relief troops out the east gate to capture you. Any day now you will lose your heads—how dare you seize my maidservants?

sentences.zh: 」賊意其夫人也，解前所執數人，獨輿妙善出城。

translations.literal: " The rebels took her for the lady and released those they had seized earlier, but alone carried Miaoshan out of the city in a palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels took her for the prefect's wife. They released those they had seized earlier and carried Miaoshan alone out of the city in a palanquin.

sentences.zh: 適所驅隸中，有盛豹者父子被掠，其子叩頭乞縱父，賊許之。

translations.literal: Among the driven servants was one Sheng Bao, father and son—both captured. The son kowtowed begging release of his father; the rebels agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the servants being driven along was a man named Sheng Bao, father and son, both taken captive. The son kowtowed and begged for his father's release, and the rebels agreed.

sentences.zh: 妙善曰：「是有力，當以舁我，何得遽縱。

translations.literal: Miaoshan said: "That man has strength—he should carry my litter. Why release him so soon?
translations.idiomatic: Miaoshan said, "That man is strong—he should carry my litter. Why release him so soon?

sentences.zh: 」賊從之。

translations.literal: " The rebels complied.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels complied.

sentences.zh: 行數里，妙善視前後無賊，低語豹曰：「我所以留汝者，以太守不知印處，欲藉汝告之。

translations.literal: After several li, Miaoshan saw no rebels ahead or behind and whispered to Bao: "The reason I kept you was that the prefect did not know where the seal was—I wanted to use you to tell him.
translations.idiomatic: After several li, Miaoshan saw no rebels ahead or behind and whispered to Bao, "I kept you because the prefect does not know where the seal is—I wanted you to tell him.

sentences.zh: 今當令汝歸，幸語太守，自此前行遇井，即畢命矣。

translations.literal: Now I will have you sent back. I pray you tell the prefect: from here forward, whenever you meet a well on the road ahead, there my life will end.
translations.idiomatic: Now I will have you sent back. Please tell the prefect: from here on, wherever you meet a well along the road ahead, there my life will end.

sentences.zh: 」呼賊曰：「是人不善舁，可仍縱之，易善舁者。

translations.literal: " She called to the rebels: "This man is poor at carrying—release him again and get someone better at carrying.
translations.idiomatic: " She called to the rebels, "This man is poor at carrying—release him again and find someone better.

sentences.zh: 」賊又從之。

translations.literal: " The rebels again complied.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels again complied.

sentences.zh: 行至花塢遇井，妙善曰：「吾渴不可忍，可汲水置井傍，吾將飲。

translations.literal: When they reached Huawu and came to a well, Miaoshan said: "I am unbearably thirsty—draw water and set it beside the well; I will drink.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Huawu and came to a well, Miaoshan said, "I am unbearably thirsty—draw water and set it beside the well. I will drink.

sentences.zh: 」賊如其言，妙善至井傍，跳身以入，賊驚救不得而去。

translations.literal: " The rebels did as she said. Miaoshan reached the well's edge and threw herself in. The rebels were startled, could not rescue her, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels did as she said. Miaoshan reached the well's edge and threw herself in. The rebels were startled, could not save her, and departed.

sentences.zh: 豹入城告榮取印，引至花塢，覓井，果得妙善屍。

translations.literal: Bao entered the city and told Rong to recover the seal; he led them to Huawu, searched for the well, and indeed found Miaoshan's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Bao entered the city and told Rong to recover the seal. He led them to Huawu, searched for the well, and found Miaoshan's body.
